Menda remembered her. After all, the previous day Menda had watched Jain cause a disturbance and get hauled away to the sanatorium. Cadric had helpfully used the incident to reinforce his earlier claim that Jain was mentally unstable.

“See? I told you!”

Now Jain was back, looking for a room.

A room at the Salty Dog normally cost copper. For Jain, Menda wanted four gold. Jain argued unsuccessfully. Jain decided to leave and go to the Blackard. Before walking out the door, she left a gift for Menda in the form of a fart.

A halfling outside caught the attention of Menda.

“See? I told you!” Cadric said again.

Some jokes were worth repeating.

Bia, however, went to the Garrison and entered just as Captain Kilm was leaving. They set up a meeting at the Mayor's office for 1:00 PM the next day to debrief.

Inside the garrison, Dr. Dave was badly burned and on morphine. Peter was awake but didn't understand where he was. His last memory was going to work several hours ago.

There'd be no additional information from either of them tonight. Bia returned to the Blackard.

docs.title: An early morning drink
docs.text:
Cadric had gone to bed before the others, which meant he also finished his long rest first.

While the rest of Ravenlost was still asleep, Cadric went downstairs at the Blackard. Henry Loust was already there with an ale in front of him.

"You called?"

Cadric got one for himself and sat down. He had indeed called and had something Henry needed to know. Dr. Caroline was dead.

More specifically, Cadric expected that Dr. Caroline might eventually become one of the ghosts at the House on Griffin Hill. If she did, Ravenlost wanted information from her about what had been happening at the sanatorium.

Henry couldn't promise anything. But he did know something Ravenlost didn't. Dr. Caroline and Lord Godfroy had a deal.

Godfroy had quietly bankrolled the new wing of the sanatorium. In exchange, Caroline was supposed to supply him with things he needed.

Cadric already knew what had been happening inside that new wing: brain surgery, experiments with aggression and control, and patients who emerged profoundly changed—if they emerged at all. He asked Henry if he knew exactly what Caroline had been providing to Godfroy.

Henry preferred not to know, but Cadric wasn't entirely convinced that Henry knew as little as he claimed.

But the conversation confirmed something important. The plans Ravenlost had found weren't merely evidence that Godfroy had donated money to the sanatorium. Dr. Caroline had been working with him.

Cadric had heard enough. It was time for pastries. The others would be awake soon.

docs.title: The bigger problem
docs.text:
When Ravenlost finally awoke, Jain opened the journal that she'd pilfered.

Control: A Roadmap was a sort of medical diary and a how-to guide. It was apparent that Dr. Edgar was trying to figure out how to perform surgery on a brain to make someone more susceptible to manipulation. It was dated about 40 years ago, and according to his writings, it seemed he was getting close. Also, Dr. Caroline looked to be in her 40s, making Ravenlost even more convinced that she was his daughter.

From the journals, Ravenlost also learned that Dr. Edgar had lost his funding at Locust Branch Hospital when one of his surgeries had gone bad and a patient snapped.

By now, it was nearing 1:00 PM, so the team headed out to meet with Mayor Alice and Captain O'Connell to explain what they had found.

There was quite a bit to explain. Peter had almost certainly committed the murders. The guards had the matching daggers from his quarters, and Peter's unexplained nighttime activities lined up with the attacks.

But Ravenlost no longer believed he had been acting entirely of his own free will.

Peter remembered going to work the previous evening. After that, nothing. He didn't remember leaving his post, fleeing to the docks, stabbing Bia, or being knocked unconscious against a piling.

"That went faster than I thought," Mayor Alice said to them. She was now beginning to understand how Ravenlost worked.

Ravenlost showed Dr. Edgar Iskander's journal to Captain O'Connell and the Mayor. The doctor's research described ways of manipulating the brain to affect memory, aggression, and susceptibility to commands. Peter's behavior looked disturbingly similar to the effects described in the journal.

The orderlies offered even more evidence. Captain O'Connell confirmed that they didn't speak. More importantly, every one of them had identical scarring around the top of the skull.

He also provided them with more information about Peter. Peter had surgical incisions behind his ears.

Ravenlost had seen the surgical rooms. They were beginning to understand what they'd been used for.

Dr. Dave was different. He had arrived at the sanatorium with Dr. Caroline, worked alongside her in the ICU, and had actively fought Ravenlost to protect what they were doing. Whatever had happened to Peter and the orderlies, there was no indication Dr. Dave was another unwilling participant.

The captain also informed them that the body in the morgue was Anne Polk. She was known in town for her demeanor and her hysteric fits. She'd been a patient at the sanatorium for about 3 years.

And then Ravenlost told Captain O'Connell about Lord Godfroy.

The remodeling plans they had recovered showed that Godfroy had privately funded the new addition containing the ICU. Ravenlost believed Dr. Caroline had been continuing Edgar Iskander's research there, trying to perfect a way to manipulate aggression and control people—and that whatever she learned was intended to make its way back to Godfroy.

How much Godfroy knew about the individual experiments was still unclear. But this was no longer merely a suspicion based on the jobs he had been giving them. His name was on the remodel plans.

The sanatorium had started as an investigation into a few murders in Mordenshire. Somehow, once again, it had led Ravenlost back to Lord Godfroy.

Finally, Cadric asked the mayor for information on any scholars we might find in the three locations we'd be traveling to soon. She suggested that Cadric try Old Books in town and speak with the scribe, or reach out to Rudolf Von Richten. Either of them might be able to help.

With the meeting concluded, Mayor Alice asked them to meet her at her home, Weathermay House, at 7:00 PM that night to receive their reward.

docs.title: The sanatorium in daylight
docs.text:
After Ravenlost left the Mayor's office, they returned to the sanatorium, finally seeing it in daylight. It was still standing. Mostly.

Dr. Caroline was dead. Dr. Dave and Peter were in custody. Part of the building had burned. Two orderlies were dead. The remaining staff were trying to figure out what came next.

And with Dr. Van Larden now in charge, the patients were finally getting out.

When Bia had first arrived, Randal, Janice, and Robert had explained that patients who went into intensive care didn't come back. They hadn't known how literally true that warning was. But now, patients were being discharged and provided with 3 silver pieces each. And the facility that had held roughly twenty patients was now down to only a handful of patients and orderlies who still needed care.

Wendel wasn't leaving.

He had moved permanently into Dr. Caroline's quarters, and this morning he was digging in the garden. A dark-eyed doctor whom Ravenlost had taken to calling Dr. Goth was keeping an eye on him. And she was wearing plain clothes.

Wendel seemed perfectly happy digging beside someone who wasn't wearing a doctor's coat. Apparently, after everything Dr. Caroline had tried to do to him, what Wendel really needed was a garden, regular clothes, a comfy bed in a room that didn't have a surgical table, and someone willing to leave him alone for a while.

Elisandra showed Dr. Goth the journal and asked if she understood it. She had bad news and good news. The "good" news was that, when successful, the operation didn't otherwise prevent someone from living a normal life. It simply left them permanently susceptible to suggestion.

Ravenlost had different definitions of "good news."

Bia learned that Randal, Janice, and Robert had all been discharged and were currently looking for work in town. One patient, however, was still unaccounted for. Trashcan.

Trashcan had helped warn the others during the fire and then disappeared in the commotion. No one knew where he'd gone.

Elisandra and Jain went upstairs to Caroline's (now Wendel's) room to try to find any information indicating that Dr. Caroline was Dr. Edgar's daughter and any information on Trashcan. Wendel's room was a mess. The surgical table was thrown on the roof.

They found more records from Locust Branch Hospital with Dr. Edgar's name. Then Elisandra found a piece of paper from Edgar to Caroline that said, "I will always be with you." Ravenlost wondered whether "I will always be with you" might have been more literal than Edgar intended when he wrote it. If Edgar was dead, perhaps his ghost had ended up at the House on Griffin Hill. And if so, had he ever visited the sanatorium?

They found paperwork on Jain.

"Shows aggression." "Exhibits signs of submission." "She is a flight risk." "She's a perfect candidate."

They completed their investigation without finding any additional information about Trashcan. Elisandra took comfort in the realization that, somewhere in Mordenshire, there was now an unattended trash can on the loose.

Cadric found Cookie. After everything that had happened — the hemlock, the fire, the dead orderlies, the escaped patients, and the cookies that had unexpectedly become part of Wendel's treatment plan — Cadric wanted to say goodbye.

Cookie thanked him for the butter. Cadric promised there would be more, and Cookie immediately took him up on it. Cookie provided Cookie with a list of ingredients.

Bia returned to the garrison to check on the status of Dr. Dave and Peter. There was nothing new other than the Suggestion on Dr. Dave had worn off. Dr. Dave was uncooperative, and Peter was still confused.

So while the murders had been solved, what Ravenlost still didn't know was how many of them had actually been Peter's choice.

docs.title: Old Books
docs.text:
With three possible destinations and very little information about any of them, Ravenlost decided some research might be useful before choosing where to go first.

Cadric volunteered. He was already heading to town with a list of ingredients. But with this new pressing task, he instead enlisted the young Speedy to buy the ingredients and return them to Cookie.

At Mayor Alice's suggestion, Cadric then headed to Old Books, a bookstore near the market that was exactly what its name promised. The place smelled like musty paper and looked less like an organized shop than a building where someone had spent years accumulating books and piling them wherever they would fit.

Eventually, a young blonde woman with wiry hair emerged from somewhere behind the stacks.

“Welcome. My name is Gilda.”

“Cadric Veyl.” Cadric waited for a response. Gilda didn't recognize the name.

“Gilda Haywood.”

With introductions successfully accomplished, Cadric explained what he needed. Ravenlost had three leads: Welkspring House on Echo Island, the Cauldron of Tempest, and a man in Falkovnia named Mikhail Hatzimvas.

Gilda disappeared into the stacks.

She was gone for about fifteen minutes. Cadric used the time to work on his song for his gig later that night. The chorus was solid. The second verse was done. The first verse still needed help.

Eventually, Gilda returned.

She hadn't found anything useful about Mikhail Hatzimvas, but she'd had better luck with Echo Island. She found a record of the ownership of Welkspring House and a botanical guide written by its most recent owner, Osgood Escar.

The house had belonged to the Welkspring family before Osgood acquired it. More interestingly for Cadric, Osgood's botanical guide included information about hemlock, which grew naturally along the northwestern coast of Echo Island.

Cadric had recently discovered several practical applications for hemlock. Echo Island was becoming more interesting.

Gilda also found information about the Cauldron of Tempest, giving Ravenlost at least something to work with as they considered Godfroy's three leads. It wasn't enough to tell them which destination was the right one. But it was considerably more information than they'd had when Cadric walked in.

Before leaving, Cadric had one more request.

He would be in Mordenshire for another four days. If Gilda was willing, he wanted her to spend that time finding everything she could about Osgood Escar and put together a summary for him.

Gilda agreed.

Cadric paid her five silver and promised to return in four days.

Ravenlost still hadn't decided where they were going first, but by then, they should know considerably more about at least one of their options.

docs.title: Payment in kind
docs.text:
By now, it was nearing the time to meet Mayor Alice at her manor.

They found Weathermay House to the north, outside of town. Her home was a large marble manor with an adjoining mausoleum. While walking past that, it's possible one or two of the team thought, just for a moment, about "investigating" the mausoleum. But there was no time for that.

A butler let them through the locked gates and led them into a comfortable sitting room in the house. Mayor Alice was waiting for them.

Mordenshire had hired Ravenlost to investigate the sanatorium and determine whether it was connected to the murders. Technically, they had done exactly that.

They had also uncovered illegal brain experiments, exposed Dr. Caroline's arrangement with Lord Godfroy, identified the murderer, captured him alive, and helped dismantle whatever had been happening inside the ICU.

Yes, there'd been some fire damage, but Dr. Dave had started that.

Unfortunately, Alice explained to them that Mordenshire didn't have enough money available to properly reward Ravenlost for everything they'd uncovered and also rebuild the burned parts of the sanatorium. Instead, Mayor Alice offered them something else. She had three magical items.

The first was a Periapt of Health, a necklace that protected its wearer from disease. That went to Jain.

The second was a Pearl of Power, which could restore some of a spellcaster's expended magical energy. This would be useful to Elisandra.

Then Alice opened a case containing two matching daggers, one gold and one silver.

Aurum and Argentum

Both were magical +1 weapons, but they'd been designed to be used together. In the hands of someone fighting with both, the pair became considerably more effective.

Everyone looked at Cadric. Cadric took the daggers.

Bia looked at the three magical rewards that had just been distributed among the other three members of Ravenlost. There were four members of Ravenlost.

Apparently, solving the murders, helping expose a brain-control operation, chasing Peter into the water, getting stabbed, and punching him unconscious against a dock piling didn't come with a magical item.

It still wasn't lost on Bia that none of them had been arrested for manslaughter. Considering how the investigation had gone, she was willing to count that as her reward.

And another reward was Cadric's upcoming gig.

docs.title: A paying gig
docs.text:
After leaving Weathermay House, Ravenlost returned to the Blackard.

Cadric had a gig.

He'd been working on a new song for several days. The chorus was finished. He had a second verse. The first verse was still a work in progress, but eventually a bard had to stop writing and start performing.

Cadric took the stage.

His song followed the adventures of a wandering halfling who could find a home anywhere—and generally leave that home with more money than he'd arrived with.

The chorus was catchy:

Oh the wandering halfling, wherever he may roam, He’ll find a warm fire and call it his home. With a song in his heart and a coin in his shoe, He’ll steal your heart first, and all your coin too.

One verse featured an orc with an axe six feet long who was extremely confident that no thief could get the better of her. But the halfling got the better of her.

Bia listened.

Apparently, Ravenlost was becoming material.

Cadric accompanied the song with magical images, creating a little cottage and then bringing the audience inside as the story unfolded.

It went over well. Very well, in fact.

Cadric had already performed at the Blackard before, but this time he was beginning to look less like a traveler who happened to own a lute and more like part of the evening's regular entertainment.

And he wasn't finished. Ravenlost would be staying in Mordenshire for several more days.

Cadric had more performances scheduled. And, apparently, more verses to write.

docs.title: Three quiet days
docs.text:
For the next three days, Ravenlost remained in Mordenshire.

Nothing caught fire. No one was murdered. Nobody infiltrated a sanatorium. Nobody robbed a mausoleum.

It was surprisingly pleasant.

Bia checked in on Randal, Janice, and Robert and discovered that all three had already found work. One was working at the Blackard, another had found a job as a runner in the marketplace, and the third was working in a nearby wheat field.

The gold Bia had given them had helped them get started. They were doing fine from there.

Jain spent some of her free time climbing the cliffs around Mordenshire. Getting up was considerably easier than getting down, but that didn't stop her.

One day, after reaching the top, she looked out toward the water. Far offshore, a trash barge was slowly disappearing toward the horizon. Sitting proudly in the middle of it was a familiar trashcan.

Jain watched until it disappeared from view. Trashcan was fine. Probably.

She didn’'t tell the others.

Elisandra, meanwhile, had acquired a raven. She spent part of the next few days hanging out with her companion and trying to teach it to talk. Progress was slow, but Elisandra was committed.

Cadric had considerably more public plans. He continued performing at the Blackard each night. His first performance had gone well. The next three went even better. By the end of his run, Cadric had earned 16 gold worth of silver from his performances.

More importantly, people kept coming back to hear him.

For a few days, Ravenlost almost looked like a group of ordinary travelers enjoying some downtime in Mordenshire.

Almost.

They still had three assignments from Lord Godfroy, a suspiciously useful sword sitting inside a Bag of Holding, equipment waiting to be collected, and a researcher at Old Books who had been spending the last several days investigating Osgood Escar.

Eventually, the quiet days ran out. Cadric returned to see Gilda.

docs.title: Back to Old Books
docs.text:
Four days after his first visit, Cadric returned to Old Books.

Gilda was ready for him. Mostly.

She was moving frantically through the shop, gathering books and notes.

"Oh, you made it back! I've been working at this for days."

She'd found considerably more information about Osgood Escar than she'd found about poisons. Osgood was a botanist of some renown who had traveled through the Mists studying unusual plants and botanical creatures. He'd eventually acquired Welkspring House on Echo Island and extensively remodeled the grounds.

That had happened 73 years ago. There was one problem with that. Osgood was human, but Gilda hadn't found any record of his death. She had, however, found several of his books. One was an Encyclopedia of Poisons of Ravenloft. Others covered his botanical research.

And several were dedicated to the same person. Glim Brightstone.

The dedications described Glim affectionately: a friend, a helper, and someone who was always at Osgood's side when he needed them. Apparently, Osgood and Glim had first met in Borca, a domain known for its unusual plant life—and its two dreadlords. The more Cadric read, the more the relationship between Osgood and Glim sounded like it might have been considerably closer than professional colleagues.

Gilda hadn't found anything connecting Osgood to Lord Godfroy. That was probably good. But she had found enough to make Welkspring House considerably more interesting.

Ravenlost had been looking for Glim Brightstone. Now they had a human botanist who had known Glim personally, had written about Glim repeatedly, had purchased a house 73 years ago, and apparently had never died.

And, conveniently, he lived on the one island where Cadric could replenish his supply of hemlock. Echo Island was looking better all the time.

docs.title: Choosing a direction
docs.text:
Ravenlost had three leads and, thanks to Gilda, considerably more information about one of them.

There was the Cauldron of Tempest, somewhere beyond the Mists and associated with stories of resurrection.

There was Mikhail Hatzimvas in Falkovnia, who ran a hospital for people suffering from the region's undead affliction.

And there was Welkspring House on Echo Island, home to a human botanist who had purchased the property 73 years ago, had apparently never died, and had known Glim Brightstone well enough to dedicate multiple books to them.

Echo Island also had one other advantage. They could get there without traveling through the Mists.

That made the decision considerably easier. Welkspring House would be first.

Before leaving Mordenshire, Ravenlost collected the various things they'd commissioned around town.

Jain picked up the silver canine caps Van Richten had made for her. They fit over her teeth, giving her a new option the next time she encountered something that didn't respond particularly well to ordinary weapons.

Jain had also left her shortsword with the blacksmith to be silvered. That process took considerably longer. Only one weapon could be done at a time, and it would take about a week. That was a problem Cadric had narrowly avoided. He'd considered having his own shortsword silvered, but instead he'd accepted the magical +1 shortsword Lord Godfroy had loaned him.

Of course, that sword also allowed Godfroy to scry on him. But it remained safely inside the Bag of Holding whenever Cadric wasn't using it.

Cadric and Elisandra also picked up their EC Lights from the blacksmith. Then they picked up their belts and Cadric's pouch from the leatherworker.

By the morning of the fourth day of quiet, Ravenlost gathered the rest of their equipment, finished their errands, and prepared to leave Mordenshire.

Now they just needed transportation.

docs.title: A ride to Echo Island
docs.text:
Fortunately, Ravenlost already knew a sailor with a boat.

Unfortunately, Jain had shot him.

They found The Fletcher tied up at the docks, but its captain was nowhere to be seen. Eventually, they tracked Jethro Fletcher to The Seventh Sea.

He was face-down on the bar, hands still wrapped around a mug. Beside him, a small goblin was happily spinning himself around on a barstool. This was Gobbo, Jethro's first mate.

Ravenlost asked Gobbo about the proper procedure for waking his captain. Gobbo swung himself sideways, raised both feet, and kicked Jethro as hard as he could.

Jethro hit the floor. He was awake.

Ravenlost had found their captain.

"Where are you trying to go?"

"Echo Island."

Jethro could do that. Better yet, reaching Echo Island didn't require traveling through the Mists.

When Ravenlost mentioned Welkspring House, however, Jethro drew a line. He would take them to the docks on the southern side of the island. He wasn't going anywhere near that house.

That worked for Ravenlost.

Jethro initially offered to take them there for free. After all, he owed them.

Ravenlost, who had recently shot him in the leg, had a somewhat different understanding of who owed whom.

They offered to pay.

Jethro asked for three cases of liquor. Ravenlost offered six.

Negotiations were going extremely well.

Eventually, they settled on six cases, costing 36 silver. Jethro would get one case before they left, two more when they reached Echo Island, and the final three after Ravenlost returned.

That gave him a reason to wait for them. It also gave him two cases of liquor while he waited.

Everyone seemed satisfied with this arrangement.

Jethro estimated that the trip would take about twelve hours, assuming the weather cooperated. Leaving that morning would put them at Echo Island sometime around 8:30 that night.

Arriving at a mostly wilderness-covered island after dark sounded like an excellent plan. At least they had lights.

Before boarding, Bia made one final trip to the bakery and bought a box of pastries for the journey.

Then Ravenlost boarded The Fletcher. Gobbo scrambled around the rigging preparing the sail, Jethro got them underway, and Mordenshire slowly disappeared behind them.

Everything seemed to be going swimmingly.

docs.title: Weather permitting
docs.text:
For the first half of the trip to Echo Island, everything went surprisingly well. The weather was pleasant. The water cooperated. The Fletcher made good time.Ravenlost had apparently found a form of transportation that wasn't going to try to kill them.

Then the weather turned.

As they approached Echo Island, the wind picked up and the waves grew rougher. Jethro struggled with the rudder as the boat began fighting against him.

He started shouting orders.

"Strong one! Take the main line!"

Bia looked at him. "What's the main line?"

They were off to an excellent start. Apparently Bia needed to have spent her down time taking sailing lessons.

Jethro pointed to the large rope coming off the sail. "That! Hold it! Don't let it go!"

Bia grabbed the line. Gobbo joined her, although "joined her" mostly meant hanging from the rope while the wind whipped him around.

Jethro put Jain and Elisandra on the rudder. Together, they fought to keep it steady as the waves tried to knock The Fletcher off course.

Cadric had an equally important job. He sang a sea shanty.

It wasn't one of his better performances.

Fortunately, everyone else's work made up for it.

Bia kept control of the sail. Jain and Elisandra held the rudder steady. Jethro somehow kept the boat pointed toward Echo Island.

Eventually, through the darkness and the storm, land appeared.

The island was mostly surrounded by cliffs. On its southern shore was something that could generously be described as a port. It had one dock. Jethro brought The Fletcher alongside it.

Ravenlost had made it to a stormy Echo Island. Alive. Again.

docs.title: Exquisite grass
docs.text:
The southern shore of Echo Island wasn't much of a settlement. There was a single dock with another small fishing boat and a few buildings clustered near the water. Beyond them was mostly wilderness.

As The Fletcher pulled in, the door of one of the houses opened. An older, weathered man in a canvas raincoat emerged carrying a shielded lantern. He hurried down to help secure the boat.

"Are you all right? You make port okay?"

Technically, yes.

The man introduced himself as Shauncey and invited everyone inside to get out of the storm and dry off.

Once they were settled, he had a reasonable question. What exactly had brought them to Echo Island?

"Just sightseeing."

Shauncey looked confused.

"What sights?"

"The trees. The rocks. The whole island."

Jain considered this. "Grass. I'm a fan of grass, and I've heard there's exquisite grass here."

This didn't appear to answer Shauncey's question.

Ravenlost tried another explanation. They were a traveling troupe of circus performers.

That worked considerably better. Cadric was the entertainer. Jain could climb pretty much anything. Elisandra was new, and she was still teaching her bird to talk. And Bia could toss logs.

Shauncey was delighted. He wanted to see an act. Ravenlost had just survived a twelve-hour boat ride that ended in a storm, but Shauncey had given them shelter.

So Cadric performed. He even gave Shauncey the second verse of his new song.

Whatever doubts Shauncey might have had about the strange group that had arrived on his doorstep disappeared. By the end of the evening, he was a Cadric fan.

Ravenlost spent the night at his house. Everyone was tired, and no one bothered keeping watch. Thankfully, nothing happened. And for once, that was actually true.

By morning, the storm had passed. When Ravenlost asked about Welkspring House, Shauncey told them it was roughly a two-hour journey inland. He didn't go that way himself anymore.

"The woods are weird now."

That was useful information.

More useful was a name. Ava had once worked as the groundskeeper at Welkspring House. She lived nearby and knew the property. If Ravenlost wanted to know what they were walking into, they should talk to her.

docs.title: The former groundskeeper
docs.text:
Before setting out, Ravenlost took advantage of Shauncey's hospitality for breakfast. Shauncey supplied the small settlement with fish and offered everyone one smoked fish for free. There were also some pastries left over from the previous day.

Then Ravenlost went looking for Ava. They found her near her log cabin, felling a tree.

Ava was muscular, with short brown hair, and looked entirely capable of taking care of herself. More importantly, she'd once been the groundskeeper at Welkspring House.

She didn't work there anymore. According to Ava, she'd been told to stay away for her own safety. She'd even been given approximately a year's wages when she left.

That got Ravenlost's attention.

For about the last six months, Ava had occasionally noticed strange figures moving through the woods at the edge of her vision. She could never get a good look at them. Sometimes they appeared small. Sometimes tall and thin. Sometimes somewhere in between, but broader. They never stayed around long enough for her to determine what they were, and they didn't leave tracks behind.

Ava hadn't returned to Welkspring House since leaving. She could, however, tell Ravenlost how to get there. There were two options.

They could follow the established route through the woods. It would take longer, but it was safer.

Or they could take a more direct route through the forest. It was faster. It was also considerably more likely to put them in the path of whatever had been moving through the trees.

Ravenlost considered these options.

They decided to take the shortcut.

Of course they did.

docs.title: The shortcut
docs.text:
The shortcut began pleasantly enough. Echo Island was covered in a thick, temperate forest. Sunlight filtered through the trees as Ravenlost worked their way north toward Welkspring House.

After a while, Jain noticed something. Or more accurately, she noticed nothing. The forest was silent. No birds. No animals moving through the undergrowth. Nothing except the wind through the trees.

Then Jain caught a glimpse of something humanoid peeking around a tree ahead of them. It disappeared almost immediately.

Ava's warning suddenly seemed considerably more relevant.

Cadric tried a bird call. It was actually quite good.

Something answered him. With a thorn.

The projectile buried itself in the side of Cadric's neck. So much for the birds.

More figures then emerged from the trees. Some were smaller humanoid shapes covered in needles and thorns. Others were larger creatures formed from twisting vines.

Ravenlost fought back.

The smaller creatures fired volleys of needles from the surrounding woods. One of the larger creatures lashed Elisandra with vines. Bia struck another hard enough to sever its arm. The vines immediately began slowling growing back.

"Guys, I just cut off one's arm and it's growing back."

That was useful information.

The fight continued as more of the creatures emerged from the trees. Ravenlost killed several of them, and eventually the survivors decided that whatever they'd hoped to accomplish wasn't worth dying for.

They scattered back into the forest. Ravenlost let them go.

About half an hour later, they finally reached a clearing.

Twenty feet ahead stood an eight-foot wrought-iron fence, with tall, carefully maintained hedges rising behind it.

They'd found Welkspring House.

"I think we made it, guys," said Jain. Aren't you glad we took the shortcut?"

Cadric pulled the three-inch thorn out of his neck and put it in his bag.

"We've all gotten a splinter before."

Apparently, the shortcut had been a success.

docs.title: A familiar design
docs.text:
Beyond the wrought-iron fence, Ravenlost found an open gate. That was either welcoming or concerning.

Inside, a winding path led through immaculate gardens toward an enormous estate. The manor itself was impressive, but beside it stood something even larger: a massive greenhouse packed with greenery.

Off to one side was a carefully maintained topiary garden filled with animals. Jain considered investigating it. Cadric considered whether the topiary animals might come alive and attack them.

They decided to leave the topiaries alone. For once, restraint won.

They followed the path to the manor instead. The front entrance stood above a raised porch reached by two staircases. Ravenlost climbed the steps and knocked on the large French doors.

From inside came a voice. "Just a minute." Then came the unmistakable whirring of machinery.A small figure slowly opened the door.

It was an automaton, only about three and a half feet tall, with a humanoid upper body mounted on a ball instead of legs.

Every member of Ravenlost had the same thought.

Cedgewick.

It obviously wasn't Cedgewick. But the construction was familiar enough to immediately remind them of the automaton they'd found in Glim's laboratory.

"How can I hel hel help you?" it stuttered.

Ravenlost explained that they were there to see Osgood Escar.

"Mmm master is up up upstairs."

The automaton told them it would be right back. Then it rolled over to the staircase. And ran directly into the bottom step.

Thump.

It tried again.

Thump.

And again.

Thump.

The metal ball beneath it was extremely effective for moving across a flat floor. It was less effective at stairs.

Eventually, a voice called down from above.

"Just give me a moment."

The automaton stopped trying to climb. Ravenlost waited.

After several minutes, they heard a cane strike the floor upstairs. Then a footstep. Then the cane again. Someone was coming down.

docs.title: Laying the cards on the table
docs.text:
The man coming down the stairs introduced himself as Osgood Escar. He couldn't have been older than his late fifties. He had salt-and-pepper hair, an eye patch, and clothes that looked like they'd seen considerably more gardening than laundry. His left leg was badly gnarled, forcing him to walk with a cane.

His right hand was missing. In its place was a bright silver mechanical hand. Ravenlost noticed that.

They also noticed that Gilda's research said Osgood Escar had purchased Welkspring House 73 years ago. Osgood looked nowhere near old enough for that to be possible. Nobody mentioned it.

"Somebody summoned me. How can I help you?"

Everyone looked at Cadric.

"Why are you all looking at me?"

"You're the talker."

Cadric sighed.

"Yes, we were sent here by Lord Godfroy."

Osgood's demeanor changed immediately. This was going well.

Cadric decided honesty was probably their best option.

“I'm telling you this because I'm thinking it might be helpful for us to just lay cards on the table. It's possible that we came across a lab that once belonged to Glim, and we are aware of the fact that certain people, Lord Godfrey, are interested in obtaining information about and his inventions. The reason we're here today is because we're supposed to help Lord Godfrey procure one of those items, most likely to be used in some incredibly horrendous manner to his benefit and the detriment of everyone else around.”

Osgood had a question.

“And are you intending to help him? Because you didn't say you weren't. You just said you were working for him.”

Cadric continued. “My research has told me that you are in fact a friend of Glim’s.”

Osgood's lips curled up at the corners. “You can say that.”

“We also know that Glim is missing.”

“Yes, he has been for quite some time.”

“And we know, based on what we uncovered, that he was heading north of Abbey Point.”

Again, Osgood questioned whether Ravenlost actually intended to help Lord Godfroy.

That was harder to answer.

Ravenlost explained that working for a dreadlord was complicated. They weren't particularly interested in helping Godfroy, but they also weren't particularly interested in becoming his enemies. They mostly winged it.

“We've been fortunate enough to skirt the edges, and we're hoping to continue that.”

Osgood wasn't reassured. He summarized the situation back to them.

“So I'm going to repeat as I understand. You are here at the behest of the dreadlord, to gather information about a friend of mine that I haven't seen in decades, and you aren't confirming or denying whether you intend to work with that dreadlord for whatever his purposes may be. Am I incorrect?”

That was, unfortunately, accurate. Then Cadric remembered another detail.

“His interest is specifically in an augmented version of the battery systems that are used to power the automatons that Glim designed. We’ve seen this before.”

They told him about the Glim-related device at Candle Cross, capable of releasing the Mists around the town. They told him about the machinery in Glim's laboratory that appeared capable of charging batteries. They explained that despite repeatedly finding things Godfroy might want, they had never been particularly successful at actually giving him those things.

“So again, we've never really successfully given Lord Godfrey everything that he was hoping for.”

This was somehow part of their argument in favor of trusting them.

Then they told Osgood something else he hadn't known.

Godfroy's attention was already fixed on Welkspring House. If Ravenlost returned with nothing, Godfroy could simply send someone else. Someone more capable. And possibly considerably less honest.

This sounded like a threat to Osgood, but Cadric tried to reassure him.

“I was absolutely not trying to threaten you. Look, we've had a week. It's been a long week, and I have no interest whatsoever in creating more enemies right now. And frankly, you seem like a decent fellow. So our goal here is not to create animosity. Again, we're giving you information that you didn't have 15 minutes ago.”

Then, Cadric offered something more concrete.

Godfroy had loaned him a magical shortsword. Ravenlost had discovered that Godfroy could use it to scry on Cadric. So they kept it inside the Bag of Holding.

"If we really, truly were working for the Lord, we would probably have that out."

Then came the closest thing Ravenlost had to a straightforward answer.

Did they work for Lord Godfroy? Yes. In the sense that Godfroy had sent them here. Did they want to help him return to life so he could inflict death and misery on everyone around him? No. They were fairly certain that was exactly what he intended to do with whatever he was building.

They just hadn't figured out how to stop him yet.

Osgood took a long breath. Then he stepped aside.

"Come inside."

Ravenlost had apparently passed.

"But don't touch anything."

That seemed fair.

Ravenlost entered Welkspring House.

And for now, this was a victory.

docs.title: The secrets of the silver mine
docs.text: An abbey without ale, a forest full of spiders, a soldier with unfortunate news, and a mine full of things that refuse to stay dead. Ravenlost really needs to find a better travel agent.

docs.title: A night at the abbey
docs.text:
The boat brought Ravenlost to Abbey Point after dark. From the shore, a steep path of shale steps climbed toward an abbey overlooking the coast. The well-light abbey was backdropped by the mists in the distance.

Captain Jethro Fletcher remained aboard his vessel, leaving his first mate, Gobbo, to accompany Bia, Cadric, Jain, and Elisandra up the path. Before leaving, the party promised Fletcher a barrel of ale from the abbey. It seemed like a reasonable arrangement. Surely an abbey would have ale.

Unfortunately, Ravenlost was about to discover two things about the monks of Abbey Point.

First, they had sworn vows of silence.

Second, the abbey was completely dry.

No ale. No wine. Not even something conveniently described as medicinal alcohol. Fletcher's promised barrel was looking increasingly unlikely.

At the entrance, Ravenlost encountered Davos, a monk who communicated through sign language. Luckily, Bia was fluent in sign language.

Davos offered to provide food and shelter for the travelers. He also provided more information about the abbey. The abbey was home to seventeen monks devoted to Ezra, the Lady of the Mists.

He led the visitors to a room where they were given stew, bread, milk, blankets, and pillows. It was a welcome change from sleeping aboard the boat, even if the hospitality came without a single drop of ale.

Ravenlost had not come merely for shelter. Lord Godfroy had sent them to investigate Glim Brightstone, and the abandoned silver mine in the mountains might hold information about his activities.

The monks knew the mine. They also knew the surrounding forest was dangerous.

Davos informed them that for roughly the last two years, giant spiders had occupied the woods. Creatures also sometimes emerged through the mists, and the monks rarely ventured far from the abbey.

He left them to sleep and promised to introduce them to their Abbot in the morning. He also informed them that they could not venture anywhere else in the abbey, but to just knock on the door to the next room if they needed anything.

Being told not to go somewhere was the wrong thing to say to Ravenlost. They recalled the windows outside were approximately 9 feet high. They could possibly raise Cadric on Bia’s shoulders to look in. Or Jain, who’d recently practiced climbing, could try jumping and climbing to take a peek.

In the end, they decided to just go to sleep. Very un-Ravenlost-like.

docs.title: Abbot Katun
docs.text:
The following morning, the party met Abbot Katun, the elderly leader of the monastery. Like the other monks, Katun observed a vow of silence, but he was able to communicate more information about Glim and the mine than Davos.

Glim Brightstone had owned the silver mine, which was managed by a foreman named Polk. During its working years, silver was transported along the forest trail to the coast and then sent off toward Echo Island.

Glim had also visited the abbey to study writings and symbols associated with Ezra. The abbot remembered him departing for the mountains with a covered wagon carrying something concealed.

More recently, five travelers from Mordenshire had stayed at the abbey before heading toward the mine. That had been seven or eight months earlier. None of them had returned.

After answering all their questions, the abbot presented them with some sandwiches for their journey, which would take about a day and a half.

Before departing, and now that it was daylight, Ravenlost examined the stonework around the abbey's entrance. Weathered runes carved into the sword-and-shield decoration appeared to be connected to symbols associated with Glim. And in the distance, toward the min, the mists seemed to be closing in on both sides of the mountain.

The party left with provisions for the journey, a better understanding of the mine's history, and considerably less confidence in its ability to deliver Fletcher's ale.

Gobbo continued with them.

docs.title: A spider, an elk, and a goblin in a log
docs.text:
The old mining trail hadn’t been maintained in decades.

Trees and undergrowth crowded its edges, and the forest grew unnaturally quiet as Ravenlost moved deeper into it. There were no birds singing overhead, only the occasional rustle of vegetation and the sounds of the party making its way along the path.

Then they heard something struggling in the distance.

Following the noise, Ravenlost came upon an enormous web stretched between trees near a creek. Caught in its sticky strands was a large male elk.

The animal was still alive, but it was trapped so thoroughly that its attempts to escape only made it struggle harder. Its wide eyes followed the approaching adventurers.

The party decided to help.

Working through the thick webbing, they managed to free the terrified elk. But there was an obvious question. What kind of spider could build a web large enough to catch an elk?

They were about to find out.

Movement stirred in the canopy. Gobbo, apparently deciding that discretion was the better part of valor, sought refuge inside a hollow log. Unfortunately, the log proved to be both an excellent hiding place and a terrible escape route.

Gobbo became stuck. And Ravenlost was ready to run back to the trail.

With a giant spider approaching, Bia had little patience for extracting one goblin from a log. Rather than leave Fletcher's first mate behind, she picked up the entire log and ran with it away from danger. She was then able to free him safely.

Back on the trail and above them, the spider had followed them and emerged from the trees with terrifying speed. It was approximately the size of a horse.

Ravenlost turned to face it. The creature lunged from the canopy, but its attack failed to bring down the party. Jain struck it hard, and Bia helped finish the fight.

Once the enormous spider lay dead, the party took the opportunity to collect a few souvenirs. Jain recovered all eight of its legs, while Cadric collected a vial of spider goo. Because you never know when you’ll need some spider goo.

The legs and goo went into Elisandra's bag of holding, along with the party's other collected supplies.

With Gobbo freed from his log and the elk safely gone, Ravenlost resumed its journey.

They had survived one enormous spider.

Unfortunately, the forest contained considerably more webbing.

docs.title: The soldier in the web
docs.text:
Several uneventful hours later, the trail bent around a dense tangle of brambles. Beyond it, the trees were lined with silk-wrapped sacks.

Some hung from branches. Others rested near the ground. They varied enormously in size, and a thick layer of webbing stretched across the path at approximately knee height.

Rather than risk becoming trapped, the party used their torches to burn a path through the silk.

The webbing caught fire easily. As the flames spread, several of the suspended sacks dropped to the ground.

Ravenlost continued cautiously, taking care not to step on anything wrapped in silk. There was no telling what the spiders had stored inside.

Then one of the sacks began moving. Whatever was trapped inside was still alive.

Unable to ignore the movement—or their own curiosity—the adventurers carefully cut open the silk. Inside was a badly injured male soldier wearing leather armor. His shoulder bore a festering wound, and the armor on his chest displayed the insignia of a large bird's talon.

More importantly, he was still alive.

The man looked around in confusion. He thanked his rescuers and asked where he was.

His name was Ala'kir.

docs.title: News from Falkovnia
docs.text:
As Elisandra tended Ala'kir's injuries, Bia began questioning the soldier about his homeland.

Ala'kir recognized her as an orc and suspected she might be from Falkovnia. He asked whether she had been home recently.

Bia explained that she left home about six weeks ago.

Ala'kir's news was grim.

Approximately six weeks earlier, massive hordes of undead had begun sweeping across Falkovnia. The attacks were relentless, and the military had struggled to hold them back.

Ala'kir's own regiment had suffered devastating losses. By the time his soldiers reached the mists, only ten remained. When they emerged in Mordent, there were just three.

Bia wanted to know more.

"Where were you heading when you entered the mists?" she asked. "Was it an accident?"

Before Ala'kir could finish answering, Jain turned to Cadric.

"Why are we still talking to him? We rescued him. That doesn't make him our responsibility."

"Maybe Bia wants to keep him," Cadric suggested.

Jain glanced at Bia, who was still waiting for Ala'kir's answer.

"Keep him? Why?"

"Well, look at her. She's awfully chatty. Maybe she finds him attractive," Cadric said.

"Are you jealous?"

"Jealous? I'm just making an observation."

"Then why don't you ask her?"

Cadric considered this. "Maybe she's hoping to bring him along. You know, spend a little more time together."

"Or," Jain suggested, "we could just put an arrow through his head and be done with it."

“Whoa,” replied Cadric. “He’s wearing a nice looking helmet. We wouldn’t want to damage it.”

Bia turned toward them.

"Can I hear what's happening in Falkovnia first? Then you can put an arrow through his head."

Cadric nodded thoughtfully. "See? She definitely likes him."

“Wait, so you’re saying that after I put an arrow in his head, then she might be attracted to him?”

Throughout this exchange, Ala'kir had been looking from one adventurer to another, trying to understand what was happening.

Finally, he interrupted.

"Am I dead?"

"No," Bia replied. "Not yet. But if you hang around with us, you’ll probably wish you were."

Ala'kir looked considerably less reassured than she might have hoped.

"And don't make eye contact with the goblin," Cadric said, gesturing toward Gobbo, who had two of his eight knives out.

Ala'kir decided it was probably best to continue answering Bia's questions.

He described the fall of defensive positions in Falkovnia, including Fort Watten along the southern border. The undead had breached its walls, forcing survivors to retreat.

The attacks weren't limited to a single direction. Undead were advancing through the region, threatening settlements and driving survivors toward whatever fortified positions remained.

"Wait," Bia interrupted. "So they're coming from the south and heading north?"

"Both directions," Ala'kir explained.

Bia listened with growing concern. She had left Falkovnia just over six weeks earlier, right before the undead began overrunning the region. Her adoptive father, Tobin Underfoot, and her sister, Mira, were still there. Were they safe? Had the undead reached their village? Had they managed to find shelter behind the walls of one of Falkovnia's remaining strongholds?

Suddenly, Ala'kir's account wasn't merely news from home. It was news that could determine whether Bia still had a home—and a family—to return to.

Her companions, meanwhile, were still considerably more interested in whether she fancied the soldier.

And Ala'kir was beginning to wonder whether surviving the spiders had actually improved his situation.

docs.title: More trouble in the sacks
docs.text:
The group still faced the problem of the remaining silk bundles. Some appeared to contain animals. Others were large enough to hold humanoids. Could any of them be Ala’kir’s missing travel companions?

Curiosity won again.

As the party examined the different-sized fallen sacks, they discovered the remains of several unfortunate creatures, including an elk, a partially digested hobgoblin, and humanoid and canine-humanoid bones.

Then Elisandra opened a sack that contained something considerably more dangerous.

A swarm of tiny spiders spilled out. The creatures were small, but their venom was potent. They overwhelmed Elisandra, poisoning and paralyzing her before the party could destroy the swarm with magic.

The danger wasn't over.

Another large bundle contained what appeared to be a dead ogre, its body covered in spider bites.

Unfortunately, the ogre wasn't content to remain dead. It rose as an undead creature and attacked.

With Ala’kir’s help Ravenlost fought the enormous corpse. Gobbo also joined the battle, demonstrating that Fletcher's first mate was considerably more useful with a blade than he had been inside a hollow log.

The fight ended when Gobbo decapitated the undead ogre.

After the battle, the party had little interest in opening additional sacks.

They had already discovered that the forest's spiders were capable of collecting an extraordinary variety of dangerous things.

docs.title: A name from Bia's past
docs.text:
Before they separated, Ravenlost asked Ala'kir whom they should seek out when they eventually reached Falkovnia.

He recommended finding refuge within a walled settlement, particularly the stronghold at Lekar. He also provided the name of the military commander leading its defense.

Commander Korath.

Bia froze.

"What the shit?"

She knew that name. The first time she'd heard it, she was only six years old.

Her Orc village in Falkovnia had been attacked during a foggy, rainy night. Her mother, Anthea, had hidden her in a cellar with a wooden doll, telling her to remain there.

From her hiding place, Bia heard screams and the sounds of fighting. And somewhere amid the chaos, she heard someone or something speak a name.

Korath.

When Bia finally emerged two days later, her father, Voros, was dead. Her mother was missing, and the village had been destroyed.

Bia eventually found another village elsewhere in Falkovnia. After finding her alone in the woods, she was taken in by the widowed halfling Tobin Underfoot and his daughter, Mira.

For years, Bia believed the attack had been carried out by a rival orc clan. But that wasn't the only time she'd heard the name Korath.

Years later, during an attack on a farm, Bia had fought to defend the village. She had saved its people, but something about the battle had frightened several children who witnessed it.

The strange thing was that Bia couldn't remember the fight.

She could guess what had happened after seeing the carnage she left behind. She knew she'd saved the village, and she knew some of the children had been afraid of her.

But the battle itself was missing from her memory. One thing, however, had remained.

The name Korath.

Repeated again through the mist that came in.

And now, standing in a spider-infested forest in Mordent, she was hearing it for the third time. This time, it belonged to a military commander supposedly protecting Falkovnia's surviving population.

Was this the same Korath whose name she'd heard during her childhood? Was he somehow connected to the mysterious fight at the farm?

Or were these three encounters entirely unrelated?

Bia had no answers.

But with Tobin and Mira still in Falkovnia, an undead invasion threatening her homeland, and the name Korath resurfacing yet again, she had more reasons than ever to return.

docs.title: Parting ways
docs.text:
Ravenlost invited Ala’kir to join them on their journey to the mine. Knowing the impression they made, they already knew the answer. So they told him about the Abbey on the shore, which sounded like a much better option.

Gabbo also had had enough.

But one thing was missing. His captain’s treasure. Gabbo couldn’t return to the ship empty handed.

Bia had no patience for negotiating. She needed to finish this job, and then she was heading straight to Falkovnia—with or without the others. Yes, they had a job to do in Falkovnia, but she needed to know whether her family was safe. She’d already lost her parents. She couldn’t lose the family that saved her too.

To make up for the lack of ale, Bia offered Gabbo 25 gold pieces, with 10 intended for Gabbo and 15 for Captain Fletcher. It came with a warning. “When I return to Mordent, if I find out that you didn’t give Captain Fletcher his share, I will kill you myself.”

Gabbo agreed. Whether he kept his promise will remain to be seen.

Ala'kir lit a torch, and the two companions headed back through the forest.

Ravenlost continued toward the silver mine.

docs.title: The abandoned mine
docs.text:
As evening approached, the party searched for a defensible place to camp. They found a sheltered location and established watches.

The forest remained unsettlingly active around them. Strange chittering echoed in the distance, and during one watch, a humanoid figure with multiple eyes was briefly glimpsed among the trees. It resembled something disturbingly close to a spider in human form.

Fortunately, nothing approached the camp.

Later, the distant sounds seemed to move toward the mountain.

By morning, Ravenlost was ready to continue. The trail eventually brought them to the abandoned silver mine.

The entrance had partially collapsed, and old spiderwebs covered the surrounding area. Whatever had once been a busy mining operation had been left to deteriorate for decades.

Bia set to work clearing the rubble. With her strength, the party was able to reopen a passage into the mine.

While she worked, the others examined the remains of the old camp.

Weather-beaten tents had collapsed under years of rain and neglect. Crates held ruined rations and abandoned mining supplies. They found detonator materials, wire, and cord, but no explosives.

More troubling were the signs that someone had visited the mine more recently. Tracks suggested that five humanoid travelers had approached the entrance.

Were these the same five visitors who had disappeared after leaving Abbey Point?

Ravenlost had no way to know. But the evidence suggested they were following the right trail.

docs.title: The dead miners
docs.text:
Inside, the mine was dark and abandoned.

Old rails ran through the tunnels, disappearing into passages that had once carried silver ore toward the surface. Flecks of silver remained visible in the rock.

The party soon discovered that the mine had not been abandoned peacefully.

In one chamber, skeletal remains lay scattered among the debris. Eight appeared to belong to miners. Another skeleton was distinctly different: a canine-humanoid creature with a pickaxe lodged in its skull.

Whatever had happened here, the miners had fought back.

Further exploration revealed barricades, ransacked supplies, and evidence of desperate attempts to defend the mine.

Some crates bore the letters PMC. Inside were useful supplies, including detonation cord, four boxed kerosene lanterns, and rope.

Anything worth keeping went into Elisandra's bag of holding.

Then Ravenlost discovered that not everyone who had worked in the mine had truly departed.

docs.title: Klem, the ghost of the mine
docs.text:
Among the abandoned crates, the party encountered a hunched figure.

At first, it was difficult to tell what they were looking at. Then the figure revealed itself to be a ghost.

His name was Klem.

He’d been trapped in the mine for an extraordinarily long time. Fifty-eight years, seven months, and three days, to be precise.

Klem remembered the mine when it was still operating. He recalled the attack that brought its work to an end: canine creatures had invaded the tunnels, and the miners had fought desperately to survive.

Foreman Polk had taken men toward the lower levels during the attack.

Klem also remembered Glim Brightstone bringing chests and a large covered object into the mine. Glim had departed after the vault was completed.

More recently, another group had entered the mine in search of something valuable. Klem remembered them traveling toward the lower levels by elevator.

Only one had escaped, carrying a bag.

The account was especially troubling given the five travelers who had disappeared months earlier.

Klem had other concerns.

The giant spiders had arrived approximately two years ago, and he was terrified of them. He warned the party about the creatures occupying the mine, including disturbing humanoid spider beings.

He also wanted something from Ravenlost. His remains were still somewhere inside the mine.

If the party could recover them and provide a proper burial outside, perhaps Klem could finally be freed from the place where he had died.

The adventurers discussed how they might accomplish that without exposing themselves to the spiders. They also considered the dangers of releasing a ghost into the mists. Would he be confined to an eternity of servitude for Lord Godfroy? Or would he be free from that because he died so long ago?

For now, Klem's remains would have to wait. The vault was still somewhere below them. And Ravenlost had a mission to complete.

docs.title: The runaway minecart
docs.text:
The old minecart rails offered a route deeper into the workings. Unfortunately, they also concealed a trap.

As they continued through the mine, a minecart suddenly came racing down the track toward the party.

There was little time to react.

The cart hit Jain. Then Bia planted herself in its path and used her considerable strength to stop the runaway cart before it could strike Elisandra and Cadric.

The impact hurt. But the cart stopped. The party continued toward the elevator that once connected the mine's upper and lower levels.

The lift was no longer functioning. Its controls were broken, and the platform rested far below. Approximately 85 feet below.

With no reliable way to operate the elevator, Ravenlost resorted to ropes. The descent wasn’t entirely successful. Elisandra lost her grip and fell, suffering a painful landing before receiving healing.

Eventually, the party regrouped on the lower level.

The tunnels below were quiet.

That didn’t make them safe.

docs.title: The guardian of the vault
docs.text:
As Ravenlost explored the lower mine with their lit torches and EC lights, they found more evidence of the violence that had consumed it.

Numerous bodies suggested that a terrible battle had taken place here. Canine-humanoid remains lay among shattered defenses. Spears pointed inward toward a chamber, and scorch marks stained the surrounding stone.

Nearby stood three red barrels. The party had good reason to suspect they contained something explosive.

Beyond the ruined defenses was the vault. Its massive silvered door glowed with an eerie blue light. The chamber seemed to be exactly what they had been searching for.

But Ravenlost was not alone.

Polk, the mine's former foreman, still guarded the lower level.

Unfortunately, death had not relieved him of his duties. The undead foreman regarded the adventurers as intruders.

The party attempted to explain that they had come seeking information about Glim Brightstone. Polk wasn’t interested.

He attacked with dynamite.

Around him, skeletal miners began rising and entering through the stone walls to defend the vault.

Ravenlost had found Glim's secret chamber.

Now they had to survive long enough to enter it.

docs.title: Battle among the barricades
docs.text:
The lower mine erupted into chaos.

Polk attacked from behind the ruined defenses while skeletons advanced with pickaxes and clubs.

The party struggled to maneuver around the barricades, fallen debris, and explosive barrels.

Cadric used Dissonant Whispers to drive an enemy away, opening an opportunity for further attacks. Cloud of Daggers tore into the undead defenders, while the party combined weapons and magic to keep the skeletons from overwhelming them.

But Polk was a dangerous opponent.

His attacks struck hard, and the skeletons continued pressing forward.

Jain fell unconscious. Elisandra was also brought down during the fighting.

With two companions incapacitated, Ravenlost came dangerously close to disaster.

Healing magic and potions became as important as swords and spells.

Bia fought to protect the others, at one point carrying the unconscious Jain out of danger.

The battle continued through the broken defenses as the party struggled to keep its wounded members alive. Polk refused to surrender, determined to defend Glim's property even in undeath. His stubbornness proved to be his downfall when Ravenlost finally defeated him. The remaining skeletons disappeared into ash.

The chamber fell silent.

The party had survived.

Barely.

docs.title: Inside Glim's vault
docs.text:
With Polk defeated, Ravenlost finally entered the vault.

The room contained several storage chests, several damaged automatons, and a floating dais.

The dais was particularly interesting. It was clear that something large had once rested upon it. But whatever the device had been, it was gone.

The party searched for clues, including a matching three-pronged key or an unusually large battery, but found neither.

Someone had apparently reached the vault before them and removed the object. Perhaps it had been the survivor Klem remembered escaping with a bag.

Perhaps not.

The chamber also contained treasure and useful supplies.

Ravenlost recovered 400 gold pieces, which they agreed to divide into shares of 100 gold per adventurer. They also found two emeralds, two greater healing potions, an unidentified potion containing what looked like suspended gas, and a revivify kit with one diamond remaining.

Three barrels of black powder were also among the supplies recovered.

The collected items were placed in Elisandra's bag of holding, with the gold shares accounted for separately.

The party had gained valuable resources.

But the missing object on the dais suggested they were already too late to recover whatever Glim had once concealed there.

docs.title: An unexpected guardian
docs.text:
After the exhausting fight, Ravenlost decided to rest inside the vault. Jain took the first watch while Bia, Cadric, and Elisandra slept.

Unfortunately, the party had overlooked one important detail: nobody had checked whether the damaged automatons still contained batteries.

Approximately two hours into Jain's watch, one of the machines suddenly came to life. The automaton seized Jain’s leg. Behind the narrow slits of its face, a soft blue light began to glow. The rest of the party awoke to the noise.

"Warning, intruders. On the authority of Brightstone, you must leave under threat of death."

The party tried to reason with the machine. They weren't thieves, they explained. They were searching for Glim Brightstone.

Elisandra reached into the bag of holding and showed the automaton the pendant they had received from Osgood.

The machine paused. A thin line of light passed across its glowing blue eye as it processed the information.

"Password."

Bia supplied the answer.

"Osgood."

"Password accepted."

The automaton released Jain.

A mechanism began whirring inside its chest. There was a crackling sound, like an old record beginning to play.

Then Glim Brightstone's voice filled the vault.

docs.title: Glim's final recording
docs.text:
A mechanism whirred inside the automaton's chest. There was a crackling sound, like an old record beginning to play. Then Glim Brightstone's voice filled the vault.

"This will be my last log. I'm going to give Hatzimvas my last piece, and then I'm going into the mists where those fiends can't find me."

Ravenlost recognized the name.

Mikhail Hatzimvas was the physician they had learned about at Griffin Hill. He operated a hospital in Falkovnia, treating those afflicted by the undead plague.

Osgood had even given the party a letter of introduction to Mikhail. Now they had another reason to find him. Whatever Glim's final piece was, Mikhail had apparently been entrusted with it.

But the recording wasn't finished.

In the background, a low whistle began to sound. It carried a strange, haunting melody—a taunting tune that seemed deliberately intended for Glim to hear.

Then Glim's voice returned, suddenly alarmed.

"God damn it!"

A wolf-like howl echoed behind him.

"They found me again. If they get me, they'll take me to Kartikoz at the old inn."

Something clattered to the ground. The recording captured the sounds of a struggle, followed by another terrible howl.

Then silence. The record stopped.

For a moment, Ravenlost had little to say.

Cadric, however, had been listening closely to the strange whistle. With his musical ear, he was able to remember the notes and write down the haunting melody.

Jain considered the howl. It hadn't sounded quite like an ordinary wolf, and she couldn't identify what had made it.

The mention of Kartikoz was also significant. It was Jain's home domain, although her fragmented memories made recalling its details difficult.

Whatever had pursued Glim, it seemed to know how to find him—even in the mists.

The automaton's blue light faded, and the machine powered down.

Ravenlost was left with several troubling questions.

Who—or what—had pursued Glim?

What was the final piece he had entrusted to Mikhail?

What had been removed from the floating dais?

And what had happened at the old inn in Kartikoz?

The party had uncovered important clues, but Glim's secret was far from solved.

docs.title: A moment of rest
docs.text:
With the automaton no longer threatening them, Ravenlost was finally able to complete its long rest. But there was still much to do.

Klem remained trapped in the mine, waiting for someone to recover his remains.

The spiders still occupied the upper tunnels.

The fate of the five travelers from Mordenshire was uncertain.

And somewhere beyond the mists, Mikhail Hatzimvas might possess the missing piece of Glim's work.

Cadric, meanwhile, had been composing another verse of his song about Ravenlost.

The latest verse was dedicated to Elisandra.

But he had no intention of performing it for free.

He decided to save the fourth verse for the next large town, where a proper audience might appreciate his work—and perhaps reward him with a few coins.

For now, the song would remain unfinished in the ears of his companions.

As the party considered its next destination, Falkovnia loomed ever larger in their plans.

There was Mikhail's hospital to investigate.

There was the undead invasion described by Ala'kir.

And for Bia, there was a name she had not expected to hear again.

Commander Korath.

A name from the night her village was destroyed. A name now attached to one of Falkovnia's most important defenders.

Ravenlost had survived the silver mine.

But the mysteries waiting beyond the mists were only beginning.

docs.title: Through the Mists
docs.text:
When the Mists offer you a shortcut, they rarely mention what “shortcut” means, and who else is traveling with you.

Ravenlost began the day deep beneath the mountains, resting inside Glim Brightstone's vault. The party had survived undead miners, discovered Glim's final recording, and collected what treasure they could carry.

There were just two problems.

The elevator was broken, and somewhere above them, giant spiders were waiting.

And, of course, they had promised a ghost they would find his body.

docs.title: The climb out
docs.text:
After a long rest in the vault, Bia, Cadric, Jain, and Elisandra began making their way out of the abandoned silver mine.

The broken elevator left them facing a climb of approximately 65 feet. Fortunately, the rope was still in place.

Everyone managed to reach the upper level, although Cadric's preferred method of climbing involved sitting partially inside the bag of holding and letting Bia lift him up.

With the party reunited above the shaft, there was one final obligation before they could leave.

Klem.

docs.title: A ghost, some spiders, and a terrible idea
docs.text:
Klem had spent more than 58 years trapped in the mine as a ghost. Ravenlost had promised to recover his remains, which were somewhere beyond the web-filled chamber. But he'd been afraid to return to his body for the last two years, ever since the giant spiders arrived.

Ravenlost needed to know more about these spiders. How many were there? How big were they? Where in the chamber were they located? Cadric tried to persuade Klem to investigate.

"Go in there and tell us where the spiders are, and come back and report," he urged.

"I won't be doing that," Klem protested.

Bia reminded him that the spiders couldn't hurt him: their attacks would pass through him, just as other objects had.

"You haven't seen them. They're really spooky," Klem replied.

Cadric eventually persuaded him, and Klem reluctantly agreed to try. The ghost drifted into the chamber while the party waited for news. Thick webs covered the room, stretching upward toward a ceiling some 30 to 40 feet high. An opening near the top suggested that creatures could enter or leave from above.

Klem spotted something moving among the webs. A spider the size of a horse dropped from the ceiling and lunged toward him. Its attack passed through the ghost, and the creature landed hard on the ground.

Klem returned to the party in a panic, confirming that at least one enormous spider was waiting inside.

Ravenlost considered its options. They had explosives. They had a minecart. They had a ranger and an orc who might be able to communicate with creatures. And they had Bia and Jain, who were willing to try almost anything once.

In the tunnel leading toward the chamber, Elisandra enchanted some stones with a Light cantrip. Bia threw them into the chamber, and the room lit up. The magical light revealed the full horror of the chamber. Thick webs coated nearly every surface, stretching from wall to wall and rising toward the high ceiling. The strands shimmered silver in the light, giving the entire cavern the appearance of a vast, glistening cocoon. Somewhere above, in the darkness beyond the light, enormous spiders waited.

Cadric snuck in to investigate. He saw a strange spider-like creature investigating one of the glowing stones Elisandra had thrown inside. It wasn't one of the enormous horse-sized spiders Klem had encountered. This creature was smaller, with four limbs and humanoid characteristics. "Nope. I'm out," he said, returning to the tunnel.

Jain slipped on her Necklace of Disguise, using its magic to take on the appearance of one of the spider-like humanoids. She then noticed three other creatures: two giant spiders and another spider-like humanoid.

Bia attempted to sneak into the chamber, but stealth was not her strongest skill. Unable to hide, she used Beast Sense in an attempt to communicate with a smaller spider-like creature. Unfortunately, the creature wasn't an animal. It responded with chittering, and no meaningful conversation followed.

With their focus turned to Bia, Jain tried an altogether different approach, putting on a seductive performance intended to distract the spider-like creatures. Whatever she hoped to accomplish, the creatures were unimpressed. Apparently, even Jain's considerable talents had their limits.

At this point, subtlety had largely ceased to be an option.

docs.title: The battle in the webs
docs.text:
Jain attempted to shove one of the giant spiders backward into its own web. The maneuver nearly worked, but the spider caught a secure strand and pulled itself to safety. She also unleashed a howl that hindered several enemies.

Elisandra entered and saw three spider-like humanoids, one of whom was Jain in disguise, and two giant spiders. It took her a moment to determine which creature was Jain in disguise. Her exaggerated chest gave her away. She then struck the spiders with a fire-based Chromatic Orb, sending flames through the web-filled chamber.

The battle was dangerous, but Ravenlost eventually gained the advantage. The two giant spiders were killed. The remaining creatures suffered injuries and attempted to escape. Rather than pursue them deeper into the mine, the party allowed them to flee.

With the chamber finally quiet, Ravenlost could return to its original purpose.

docs.title: Klem's last request
docs.text:
Elisandra's Chromatic Orb helped clear away many of the webs. At the back of the chamber, Ravenlost found the pile of rubble that had killed Klem. Bia told Cadric to let Klem know the chamber was safe, then she began moving the pile of heavy boulders.

Klem's body had been crushed so thoroughly that most of his bones had become dust. Only his legs remained recognizable. Nearby, the party discovered a silver dowsing rod. Klem explained that he'd been using it to search for valuable minerals. He had found mostly silver, along with some salt.

Ravenlost kept the rod because you never know when you'll need a dowsing rod.

The party scooped Klem's remains into a minecart and transported them out of the mine.

Outside, Klem approached what was left of his body.

“That should work.”

And "poof!" he vanished.

After more than half a century trapped underground, Klem was gone. Whether his spirit had finally found peace, Ravenlost couldn't know. But they kept their promise.

docs.title: Into the Mists
docs.text:
With the mine behind them, Ravenlost turned toward Falkovnia. They still had a mission: find Mikhail Hatzimvas and try to learn more about Glim's whereabouts.

For Bia, the journey was also personal. News of an enormous undead invasion had reached her only recently. Her adoptive father, Tobin Underfoot, and her sister, Mira, were somewhere in the threatened land. On top of that, the name "Commander Korath" continued to trouble her.

It was time to enter the Mists again. The party tied themselves together, and Jain, as a Mistwalker, led the way.

Visibility quickly fell to approximately 20 feet. The air grew colder, and the landscape began changing around them. After about an hour, the temperature dropped roughly ten degrees. The party continued walking through the strange silence.

Hours passed. Eventually, the familiar forest gave way to a bleak landscape of wind-blasted grasses, scattered trees, and muted colors.

After approximately eight hours of travel, Jain spotted a ruined barn. It looked like a possible place to rest. But Ravenlost wasn't taking any chances. Elisandra cast Augury, asking whether staying the night inside the barn would be wise.

The answer was unfavorable.

Naturally, Ravenlost went inside anyway. It wasn't night yet, after all.

docs.title: The boy in the barn
docs.text:
The barn was badly deteriorated, with a damaged roof and signs of long abandonment. Inside lay the body of a cow, dead for approximately six to eight weeks. Its remains bore bite marks.

Bia then noticed small cloven footprints on the ground, approximately the size of Cadric's feet.

Above them, something moved in the hayloft. Ravenlost looked up and saw a small head with blond curly hair.

"Are you lost, buddy?" Jain asked.

"Where are you from?" the boy asked as he emerged.

"And what's your name?" Jain asked.

"My name is Matteo. I'm from Aerie," the boy answered.

He was frightened, hungry, and alone. Ravenlost offered him food and water.

Matteo was eleven years old and came from a settlement in southern Falkovnia. He'd been hiding for the last nine days. He told them that his parents and seven-year-old twin sisters, Susie and Haley, had been separated from him while the family fled an undead attack and entered the Mists. He'd survived with limited food and water from a trough.

The party fed him, shared what supplies they could, and began asking what had happened.

docs.title: A country overrun
docs.text:
Matteo described undead creatures unlike anything he had previously encountered. Zombies had appeared in overwhelming numbers. There were undead ogres, undead birds, and other horrors moving through the countryside.

His family had been attacked while trying to escape. He explained that survivors were being directed toward Lekar, where Commander Korath controlled the defenses. The city was protected by enormous walls and the Red Gate.

But Matteo's description of Korath was hardly reassuring. The commander ruled with an iron fist, and her Talons enforced strict discipline. Conscription into Falkovnia's military could begin as young as fourteen. Farmers, however, were exempt given the recent shortage of food.

Bia listened carefully. She had left Falkovnia only about six weeks earlier. Much of what Matteo described had happened after her departure.
