docs.text: If the portrait depicts Lady Waterford, does the party need to find her remains? Does “home” mean returning her—or the portrait—to the Waterford family tomb?

docs.title: Farrow's Third Task
docs.text: What is the task Farrow refused to reveal? Could it have something to do with Lady Waterford, the portrait, or her missing body?

docs.title: The Magical Face Stone
docs.text: What exactly did Jain take from the raven-marked medical shipment—and why was someone transporting it toward Crawford?

docs.title: Idlethorpe
docs.text: What happened to the abandoned settlement, and what did Jeremiah encounter there involving all those hands?

docs.title: The Mists
docs.text: Who are the druids near Glaston, and are they really trying to find a way through the Mists?

docs.title: Bia's notes - Home is where the horrors are
Adventure at a glance
docs.text:
• Investigated Lady Waterford’s past and learned that she was born a DeLawrence Pouchenelle and came from Idlethorp.
  • Followed Lady Waterford’s portrait to the abandoned town of Idlethorp and her family’s ruined manor.
  • Fought grotesque creatures made from stitched-together body parts and discovered they were connected to a living brain in a jar.
  • Encountered a huge stitched man who resisted whatever was controlling him long enough to remove the bolts from his neck. His final word was “Sister.”
  • Returned Lady Waterford’s portrait to its place among the DeLawrence Pouchenelle family portraits.
  • Bia destroyed the brain, causing the remaining stitched creatures to collapse.
  • Looted several magic items and potions before Jain burned down the manor.
  • Returned to Farrow and received 90 gp each as partial payment.
  • Learned Farrow’s mysterious third job may have involved retrieving the very brain Bia had just destroyed.
  • Left Waterford and headed toward Candle Cross, where the castle drawbridge reportedly moves on its own.

docs.title: Waterford
docs.text:
• Woke up still trying to figure out what Lady Waterford meant when she told Jain she wanted to go home.
  • Jain stayed in room 301 with the portrait.
  • Cadric questioned Edgar.
  • Elisandra and I talked to Renee, who owns the Globe Inn.
  • Learned:
  • Lord and Lady Waterford died in a carriage accident 64 years ago.
  • They were traveling toward Mordenshire for a gala at Godfroy's Manor.
  • Lady Waterford was a DeLawrence Pouchenelle before marrying Lord Waterford.
  • Her family was from Idlethorp.
  • Edgar checks the Waterford mausoleum regularly. There is a sealed coffin for Lady Waterford, but he has never opened it.
  • We already know her coffin is empty. So where is her body?

docs.title: Scarred ghost
docs.text:
• While Jain was alone in room 301, a scarred man came into the room.
  • He seemed surprised to find Jain there.
  • Then he walked through the wall.
  • Jain saw him heading toward the docks.
  • I stayed with Lady Waterford's portrait while everyone else went after him.
  • They found a secret gathering place under the Globe Inn. We called it the human speakeasy.
  • Didn't figure out who the scarred man was, but the group did recognize one of the ghosts as one who was in Henry Loust’s office.

docs.title: Idlethorp
docs.text:
• Headed to Idlethorp because that might be the "home" Lady Waterford wanted.
  • Red warning flags outside town.
  • Met Dave, who was warning travelers away.
  • Town has been abandoned for about 6 weeks.
  • Strange noises and shadowy creatures at night.
  • Another group went in about a week ago. Only one came back.
  • We camped outside town instead of going in at night.
  • I suggested taking out Lady Waterford's portrait to see if she reacted.
  • Jain touched the frame and suddenly ran toward the manor with the portrait.
  • She wasn't controlling herself and didn't remember running there afterward.

docs.title: Creatures in Idlethorp
docs.text:
• Attacked by creatures made from stitched-together human body parts.
  • Cadric used Daylight.
  • The creatures hated it and fled.
  • They all ran toward Idlethorp manor.

docs.title: DeLawrence Pouchenelle Manor
docs.text:
• Jain pressed Lady Waterford's portrait against the manor and asked if this was the home she wanted.
  • Jain felt warmth/contentment. Definitely the right place.

docs.title: Giant stitched man
docs.text:
• Found a stitched humanoid over 8 feet tall.
  • Two metal bolts sticking out of his neck.
  • He attacked us.
  • Elisandra spoke to him telepathically about Lady Waterford and the DeLawrence Pouchenelle family.
  • He seemed to recognize something.
  • Electricity came from the bolts and seemed to take control again.
  • Elisandra told him the bolts might be controlling him.
  • He pulled both bolts out himself.
  • Electricity arced through him.
  • He collapsed and said "Sister."
  • He died.
  • Thick, dark red sludge came out of him instead of normal blood.
  • Who was he? Whose sister was he remembering? Lady Waterford?

docs.title: Meanwhile, Jain...
docs.text:
• Jain ended up alone in the ruined ballroom.
  • Huge pile of wagons, crates, lumber, dead horses, body parts, etc.
  • Watched a torso creature crawl into the pile.
  • Jain actually decided NOT to investigate it.
  • This seems important enough to document.
  • Instead, she investigated the fireplace.
  • Found a pressure-activated hook above the fireplace mantel.
  • Climbed up and triggered it.
  • Opened a secret passage.
  • Went inside by herself, because apparently the good judgment had worn off.

docs.title: Secret rooms / laboratory
docs.text:
• Cadric picked a lock.
  • Swinging blade dropped from the ceiling and barely missed his head.
  • Heard a voice say: "Don't disturb him while he's working."
  • Found a library/laboratory.
  • Man working over the body of a dwarf with surgical tools.
  • Leon DeLawrence Pouchenelle — Lady Waterford's brother.
  • Also: living brain in a jar.
  • Brain attacked me psychically.
  • More stitched creatures surrounded us.

docs.title: Ravenlost vs. the brain
docs.text:
• I eventually smashed the brain's jar with my axe.
  • Brain exploded.
  • All of the remaining stitched creatures collapsed.
  • Apparently the brain was controlling/animating them.
  • At the time, destroying the evil brain seemed like an excellent idea.

docs.title: Jain returns
docs.text:
• Jain came out through a bookcase connected to her secret fireplace passage.
  • Lots of dismembered body parts everywhere after the brain died.
  • Jain picked up two hands/arms.
  • Waved them around at Cadric.
  • A ring flew off one.
  • Cadric decided not to go after it and called it "the angel's share."
  • Jain then used the corpse arms to hug Cadric.

docs.title: Lady Waterford
docs.text:
• Found a wall filled with DeLawrence Pouchenelle family portraits.
  • One empty spot.
  • Lady Waterford's portrait fit perfectly.
  • Jain put her back with her family.
  • Jain felt the warmth/contentment settle. Lady Waterford finally seemed satisfied.
  • Still don't know where Lady Waterford's body is.

docs.title: Magic items
docs.text:
• Cadric
  • Cloak of Many Fashions
  • Instrument of Illusions
  • Bia
  • Boots of False Tracks
  • Elisandra
  • Eyes of Minute Seeing

docs.title: Potions
docs.text:
• Cadric — Potion of Growth
  • Bia — Potion of Giant Strength
  • Elisandra — Potion of Fire Breathing
  • Jain
  • Potion of Animal Friendship
  • Potion of Resistance
  • Scent of the Mists

Jain identified the potions by tasting them. Of course she did.

docs.title: Goodbye, manor
docs.text:
• Jain set the manor on fire.
  • Left Idlethorp and headed back to Waterford.

docs.title: Farrow
docs.text:
• Returned to collect our reward.
  • We were supposed to retrieve:
  • Lady Waterford's portrait.
  • Lord Waterford's jeweled walking stick.
  • We returned with neither, as far as Farrow knows.
  • Portrait stayed at the DeLawrence Pouchenelle manor.
  • Got 90 gp each as partial payment.
  • Farrow finally told us about the third job:
  • Client wants an object of power.
  • Small enough to fit in a hand.
  • We'd know it when we saw it.
  • We think it might have been the brain.
  • The brain I smashed.
  • Oops.

docs.title: Next: Candle Cross
docs.text:
• Leaving Waterford.
  • Heading toward Mordenshire through Candle Cross.
  • Candle Cross is built in the ruins of an old castle along the Arden River.
  • Its drawbridge supposedly raises and lowers by itself.
  • Some people think it reacts when evil threatens the town.

docs.title: Discoveries
docs.text: • Glim Brightstone connection: The clockwork ballerina on the fountain in the DeLawrence Pouchenelle manor had a plaque that read, “For my friend of a like mind, happy birthday, Glim Brightstone.” Someone in this family knew Glim personally. We later found a dwarf body in the laboratory. We still don’t know whether that dwarf was Glim, or who Glim’s mysterious assistant was.

docs.title: Things we still don't know
docs.text:
• Where is Lady Waterford's body?
  • Who was the scarred ghost in room 301?
  • Who was the giant stitched man, and who did he mean by "Sister"?
  • What exactly was happening in the DeLawrence Pouchenelle laboratory?
  • Was the dwarf on the lab table Glim Brightstone?
  • Was the brain actually the object Farrow's client wanted?
  • Who is Farrow's client?
  • What happens if Farrow finds out we destroyed the object?
  • What's controlling the drawbridge at Candle Cross?

docs.title: Bia's notes - The Child of Iron
Adventure at a Glance
docs.text:
The party left Waterford and continued north toward Mordenshire, stopping in Candle Cross as a storm approached. What should have been an overnight stop became much more complicated when the party discovered that the people of Candle Cross worshipped Elisandra as the Child of Iron.

By morning, the town was completely surrounded by the Mists. The party eventually discovered a strange device on the roof of the keep that could pull the Mists into a glass orb. Beneath the keep, they also found a hidden cavern containing six crowned bodies and an altar.

After Jain destroyed the orb, the Mists disappeared and the people of Candle Cross were forced to reconsider everything they had been taught about the Child of Iron. Ravenlost left the following morning, heading north toward Mordenshire with a new invitation from Henry Loust to meet Lord Godfrey at the House on Griffin Hill.

docs.title: Leaving Waterford
docs.text:
• Farrow received the portrait from Cadric.
  • The party did not give Farrow Lord Waterford's jeweled cane.
  • Farrow had already paid each party member 90 gp for completing one of his two tasks.
  • Ravenlost continued north toward Mordenshire.
  • Beyond Mordenshire is Abbey Point, where Glim reportedly went with the mysterious draft.

docs.title: Cooper
docs.text:
On the road, we encountered Cooper, whose wagon needed repairs.

  • Cooper was transporting empty barrels south toward Waterford.
  • Bia helped make a temporary repair to his wagon.
  • Cadric gave Cooper 2 cp to deliver to Farrow.
  • The money was apparently compensation "for our troubles."
  • A dark storm was approaching from the north, so everyone quickly continued on their way.

docs.title: Candle Cross
docs.text:
We reached Candle Cross, a fortified town surrounded by farmland, a river, a moat, high walls, and a drawbridge. A large keep overlooked the town.

Before entering, Elisandra used her necklace to disguise herself. She changed her white hair to black and altered her nose.

That turned out to be a good idea.

docs.title: The Child of Iron
docs.text:
In the center of Candle Cross stood an enormous statue, approximately 30 feet tall, depicting a young woman who looked remarkably like Elisandra.

The statue:

  • wore an iron crown;
  • stood above a platform containing an iron throne;
  • was acknowledged or prayed to by people passing through the square.

Elisandra finally explained some of her history.

  • Elisandra grew up in Candle Cross.
  • The people called her the Child of Iron.
  • They believed she protected the town.
  • She had no known father, which contributed to the religious beliefs surrounding her.
  • She fled Candle Cross 10 years ago, when she was 18.
  • The town continued worshipping her after she disappeared.
  • Her childhood friend and companion Adelaid helped her understand that the way Candle Cross treated her was not normal.
  • Adelaid helped Elisandra escape.

docs.title: Florence's Inn
docs.text:
We stayed at an inn run by Florence.

Elisandra remained hidden in the room.

Bia spent:

  • 1 cp for the room;
  • 4 cp for meals and drinks for Bia and Elisandra.

Total spent by Bia: 5 cp.

Cadric spent about an hour performing "Butterfly" and other songs on his lute. Afterward, he talked with Florence.

By morning, the drawbridge was up and Candle Cross was completely surrounded by the Mists.

docs.title: The Mists
docs.text:
The Mists had formed immediately outside Candle Cross, surrounding the town and preventing anyone from leaving.

At the morning sermon, the townspeople were reassured that the Child of Iron would protect them.

We decided to investigate.

docs.title: Pupert and Mr. Meeples
docs.text:
Jain and Cadric went to the wall.

They met a guard named Pubert.

Naturally, they introduced themselves using completely legitimate names:

  • Jain was Pupert.
  • Cadric was Mr. Meeples.

Jain attached Cadric to herself in a sort of baby-Bjorn Cadric, tied themselves to a rope, and went over the wall.

Pubert begged them not to do it.

When they explained that they were just going to investigate, he looked the other way.

docs.title: "I found you"
docs.text:
Inside the Mists, Jain heard someone calling to her.

She saw an injured female Lupine who told her:

"I found you."

Jain followed her deeper into the Mists.

Cadric did not see the same thing Jain saw. Instead, he saw what appeared to be another version of Jain.

Cadric convinced Jain to turn back, and they made it safely over the wall.

Jain wanted to try again.

This time, I went with her while Cadric stayed with Elisandra.

I remained on the wall and slowly lowered Jain on the rope until she was just inside the Mists.

Jain saw the female Lupine again. The figure was badly wounded and again said:

"I found you."

I felt a hard pull on the rope and immediately hauled Jain back up. Jain hit her head during the trip back and was injured.

Jain tried one more time.

I lowered her into the Mists again. The figure appeared directly in front of Jain.

Another pull came through the rope.

This time, I pulled up a nearly lifeless Jain.

I carried Jain to Elisandra, who healed her.

Important

Whatever Jain is seeing in the Mists seems to be specifically connected to her.

We still don't know who the female Lupine is or why she keeps telling Jain, "I found you."

docs.title: Investigating the Keep
docs.text:
We agreed that the keep was the most likely place to find answers.

Cadric applied makeup to Elisandra so she could move around outside without immediately being recognized.

Elisandra refused to enter the keep.

  • Elisandra remained outside to keep watch.
  • Jain stayed with her.
  • Bia and Cadric entered the keep and attempted to get a meeting with Vicar Kellan.

docs.title: Elder Pubert
docs.text:
Inside, Cadric and I met Elder Pubert, one of the town's priests.

He is presumably the father of Pubert, the guard on the wall.

Elder Pubert seemed much more helpful than some of Candle Cross's other religious leaders.

docs.title: Henry Loust
docs.text:
Cadric and I also unexpectedly encountered Henry Loust inside the keep.

Henry had a meeting with Vicar Kellan.

We spoke briefly with Henry before his meeting.

Henry already knew we were traveling with someone who looked remarkably like the Child of Iron. We don't know what Henry told Kellan during their private meeting.

docs.title: Adelaid
docs.text:
While Jain and Elisandra waited outside, they saw a red-haired woman run past.

Elisandra recognized her as Adelaid.

Jain followed her.

Adelaid told Jain that approximately three weeks earlier, a large glass sphere had been brought into the keep.

Since then:

  • the keep's routine had changed;
  • the Vicar and other leaders had become secretive;
  • strange fog had begun appearing;
  • something clearly wasn't right.

Adelaid could also get into the basement of the keep.

docs.title: Vicar Kellan
docs.text:
Candric and I eventually met with Vicar Kellan.

Kellan claimed that the Mists were a test of faith.

He knew Ravenlost was looking for Henry but did not provide useful answers about what was happening.

Kellan wanted Cadric and me to accompany him.

We refused.

He insisted that we remain in the library.

Then he locked us in.

Outside, Jain and Elisandra continued investigating the keep. Jain heard three robed men discussing the need to guard the building.

Ravenlost stopped asking permission.

docs.title: Breaking into the Keep
docs.text:
Elisandra cast Silence.

Cadric picked the lock.

We entered a stairway and encountered a guard.

The guard was knocked unconscious nonlethally.

Cadric later searched him and found an iron crown.

For once, Ravenlost managed to get through an entire town without murdering anyone.

docs.title: Beneath the Keep
docs.text:
A fountain in the basement concealed an entrance into a cavern.

Jain entered and discovered six humanoid figures.

Something was very wrong with them.

  • None appeared to be breathing.
  • Their feet were bound.
  • Iron crowns had been seared into them.
  • Some appeared to have been there much longer than others.

Farther inside was an altar covered in old candle wax.

On the altar sat a human skull wearing an iron crown.

Elisandra and Adelaid eventually entered the cavern to find Jain.

Something in the chamber announced that:

The savior has returned.

Jain touched the iron crown on the skull.

Nothing happened.

docs.title: The Second Floor of the Keep
docs.text: While Jain, Elisandra, and Adelaid investigated below, Cadric and I searched upstairs.

docs.title: Elisandra's Room
docs.text:
Elisandra's old room had been preserved for the ten years she had been gone.

It looked more like a museum than a bedroom.

docs.title: Vicar Kellan's Room
docs.text:
Cadric picked the lock to Vicar Kellan's room.

The lock was trapped.

Cadric took 1 poison damage.

Cadric found another iron crown.

By the end of the session, Ravenlost had collected three iron crowns:

  • Cadric collected two.
  • Cadric gave one of his crowns to Jain.
  • Elisandra took the third crown from the iron throne beneath her statue.

docs.title: The Orb
docs.text:
I headed directly to the roof.

There I found the glass sphere Adelaid had described.

The device included:

  • a large glass orb approximately five feet across;
  • rotating metal bands;
  • a lever;
  • red, yellow, and green buttons;
  • a slot containing a power source or battery.

The technology looked similar to equipment we had previously encountered in Glim's laboratory.

Cadric joined me on the roof and began experimenting with the controls.

He pulled the lever and pressed the red button.

The Mists began moving toward the keep.

Then the Mists were sucked into the sphere.

Something could be seen moving inside the captured Mists.

Whatever was in there was not something Ravenlost wanted getting out.

docs.title: The Return of the Child of Iron
docs.text:
With the Mists pulled away, the people of Candle Cross began running toward the keep.

Cadric cast Disguise Self.

Because Cadric is only three feet tall and the spell can only change his height so much, he couldn't disguise himself as the six-foot-tall adult Elisandra.

Instead, he disguised himself as an approximately 14-year-old Elisandra, and I lowered him down from the roof on a rope.

I helped convince the crowd that he was Elisandra.

The message was simple:

The Vicar brought the Mists. The Child of Iron pushed them back.

The crowd believed it.

Unfortunately, they decided they wanted to kill Vicar Kellan.

We stopped them.

Elder Pubert and others helped restrain Kellan, and approximately ten villagers agreed to guard the keep.

docs.title: Searching the Keep
docs.text:
I returned the young Elisandra’s clothes to her room.

I then searched the room and found a bedazzled Bag of Holding.

It was labeled:

Eli

I kept it overnight and gave it to Elisandra the following morning.

docs.title: Destroying the Orb
docs.text:
We needed to decide what to do with the sphere.

Elisandra cast Augury to determine whether destroying it was a good idea.

The answer was favorable.

The detained Vicar Kellan provided them with the destruction sequence:

  1. Activate the device.
  2. Lower the lever.
  3. Press all three buttons.
  4. Remove the battery.
  5. Get away very quickly.

Jain volunteered. Everyone left the roof for the safety of the ground.

Jain completed the sequence.

Then she had approximately four to six seconds to escape.

Jain jumped off the roof into the moat.

The sphere shattered into black pieces.

Something dark escaped upward.

The Mists disappeared.

I ran to the roof and looked down in the moat for Jain.

Jain was floating motionless in the moat.

I went down and pulled her from the water.

Jain was fine.

She was playing dead.

docs.title: Candle Cross After the Mists
docs.text:
With the Mists gone, Elisandra walked out of town and crossed the bridge.

Approximately 40 people followed her.

For some of them, this was apparently the first time they had ever willingly left Candle Cross.

They celebrated being free.

Unfortunately, they also continued treating Elisandra as their savior.

Everything Elisandra said seemed to become another divine teaching.

Adelaid found the entire situation hilarious.

Eventually, everyone ended up back at Florence's inn.

Elisandra told her followers to have 14 drinks each, apparently hoping they would get drunk enough to pass out and stop following her.

docs.title: Vicar Kellan and the Child of Iron
docs.text:
Vicar Kellan was placed in the stocks.

Elisandra confronted him about how she had been treated and groomed as the Child of Iron.

Kellan confirmed that he had no magic.

The town's walls were not magically protecting anyone.

Elder Pubert began encouraging the people of Candle Cross to reconsider their beliefs and understand that they could leave the town safely.

We took a long rest.

docs.title: The Next Morning
docs.text:
Candle Cross was already changing.

People were discussing:

  • leaving town;
  • traveling;
  • exploring places they had never seen.

Adelaid was packed and apparently ready to do exactly that.

I gave Elisandra the bedazzled "Eli" Bag of Holding I had found in Elisandra's old room.

We left Candle Cross and continued north.

docs.title: Henry Loust and the House on Griffin Hill
docs.text:
Outside Candle Cross, we encountered Henry Loust again.

Henry gave me a letter.

The letter grants Ravenlost access to the House on Griffin Hill, where Henry wants the party to meet his master, Lord Godfrey.

The party plans to continue north toward Mordenshire and eventually visit the House on Griffin Hill.

Henry also pointed us toward Mordenshire's market square for supplies.

docs.title: Cadric's Coin
docs.text:
Cadric showed Henry the strange coin connected to Jordan's disappearance.

The coin:

  • is tarnished silver;
  • was found wrapped in a black feather;
  • has an engraved symbol that seems to shift when Cadric isn't directly looking at it.

Henry recommended taking it to Rudolf von Richten, who runs an herbalist shop in Mordenshire and knows about monsters and the occult. The transcript also confirms that Rudolf is the monster hunter the party had previously been told about.

docs.title: Florence
docs.text: Innkeeper in Candle Cross.

docs.title: Pubert
docs.text: Guard on the wall. Met Jain as "Pupert" and Cadric as "Mr. Meeples."

docs.title: Elder Pubert
docs.text:
One of Candle Cross's priests. Helpful during the confrontation with Vicar Kellan and the aftermath.

Presumably related to the guard Pubert.

docs.title: Vicar Kellan
docs.text: Religious leader in Candle Cross who participated in the Child of Iron religion surrounding Elisandra. The strange sphere was kept inside his keep. He was eventually placed in the stocks.

docs.title: Adelaid
docs.text:
Elisandra's childhood friend, companion, and it's complicated.

She helped Elisandra escape Candle Cross ten years ago. She remained in Candle Cross and provided information about the sphere and recent changes at the keep.

docs.title: Cooper
docs.text: Man transporting empty barrels toward Waterford. Bia helped repair his wagon.

docs.title: Henry Loust
docs.text:
Ravenlost's original employer. Met twice during this session: first inside the Candle Cross keep and again after the party left town.

He gave me the letter for the House on Griffin Hill.

docs.title: Lord Godfrey
docs.text: Henry Loust's master. We have been invited to meet him at the House on Griffin Hill.

docs.title: Rudolf von Richten
docs.text: Monster hunter and occult expert who runs an herbalist shop in Mordenshire. Henry suggested that Cadric show him the mysterious coin connected to Jordan.

docs.title: Bia
docs.text:
• Spent 1 cp for a room at Florence's inn.
  • Spent 4 cp on meals and drinks for Bia and Elisandra.
  • Total spent: 5 cp.
  • Found the bedazzled Bag of Holding labeled "Eli" in Elisandra's old room.
  • Gave the Bag of Holding to Elisandra the next morning.
  • Received the letter from Henry granting access to the House on Griffin Hill.

docs.title: Iron Crowns
docs.text:
Three iron crowns were collected:

  • Cadric collected two.
  • Cadric gave one to Jain.
  • Elisandra took one from the throne beneath her statue.

docs.title: Advancement
docs.text:
No level up.

Ravenlost remains Level 3.

docs.title: The Female Lupine
docs.text:
Who did Jain see in the Mists?

Why was she badly wounded?

Why did she repeatedly tell Jain:

"I found you."

docs.title: The Mists
docs.text:
Why did the Mists suddenly surround Candle Cross?

Why did they affect Jain the way they did?

docs.title: The Orb
docs.text:
Who created the glass orb?

Who brought it to Candle Cross?

Why does its technology resemble equipment from Glyn's laboratory?

docs.title: What Was Inside the Orb?
docs.text:
What were the shapes moving within the captured Mists?

What was the dark thing that escaped when the orb was destroyed?

docs.title: The Six Crowned Figures
docs.text:
Who were the six figures beneath the keep?

Why were they bound?

Why had iron crowns been seared into them?

Why did the chamber react to Elisandra's return?

docs.title: The Iron Crowns
docs.text:
Why are there so many iron crowns?

Do the three Ravenlost collected have any significance beyond their connection to the Child of Iron?

docs.title: Henry and Vicar Kellan
docs.text:
What did Henry tell Vicar Kellan during their private meeting?

Did Henry reveal that Ravenlost was traveling with someone who looked like the Child of Iron?

docs.title: The House on Griffin Hill
docs.text:
Why does Lord Godfrey want to meet Ravenlost?

What does Henry's master need us to do?

docs.title: Cadric's Coin
docs.text:
What is the symbol on the coin found after Jordan disappeared?

Why does it seem to move when Cadric looks away?

What is the significance of the black feather?

docs.title: Glim
docs.text:
Is Glim still heading toward Abbey Point?

Is there a connection between Glim's work and the device Ravenlost found in Candle Cross?

docs.title: Bia's notes - "It wasn't me" in Mordenshire
Adventure at a Glance
docs.text:
Ravenlost finally reached Mordenshire, where we planned to sell our treasure, visit Rudolph Van Richten, and eventually meet Lord Godfroy at the House on Griffin Hill.

Our visit became considerably more complicated. We helped Van Richten contain a creature released from a mummified cat, learned more about the Mists and Glim Brightstone, discovered the fourth victim of a serial murderer, and agreed to go undercover inside Mordenshire's sanatorium.

We also finally met Lord Godfroy. He wants us to investigate three locations connected to Glim and find a larger Glim battery. He's offering 15,000 gp each, but we have to leave Mordenshire in one week.

Ravenlost reached Level 4.

docs.title: Arriving in Mordenshire
docs.text:
Mordenshire is a large, busy coastal town with a harbor.

We attracted some attention when we arrived. Apparently a halfling, an orc, a Lupine, and a Kalashtar walking into town together is “unusual.”

The guards told us about three inns:

  • Blackcard - In the center of town. Popular with merchants and conveniently located near a bakery.
  • The Seventh Sea - Near the coast/docks.
  • The Salty Dog - Near the sanatorium and popular with scholars.

Jain heard "sanatorium" and immediately wanted to stay at the Salty Dog.

docs.title: Blackcard
docs.text:
Bia and Cadric stayed at the Blackcard, Room 304.

  • Innkeeper: Alenta, an elderly Gnome.
  • Alenta had an old grimoire behind the desk.
  • Cadric agreed to perform from 8:00-9:00 p.m.
  • His performance covered our room and board.

docs.title: Salty Dog
docs.text:
Jain and Elisandra stayed at the Salty Dog, Room 213.

  • Innkeeper: Menda.
  • They checked in under the false name "Jainisandra."
  • Bia and Cadric later gave Menda a letter to pass to any guests resembling a Lupine and a Kalashtar.
  • Jain and Elisandra attempted to discreetly leave their second-story room through the window.
  • Bia, Cadric, and everyone else in the bar saw them.

Very discreet.

docs.title: Strange magic
docs.text: While we were together at the Salty Dog, we examined some of the magical items we'd collected.

docs.title: Elisandra's crown
docs.text:
Elisandra tried on a magical crown intended for a cleric.

  • The crown requires attunement.
  • When Elisandra put it on, Bia and Jain saw a vague figure appear above her.
  • It looked like a skeletal hand resting on her shoulder.
  • The figure disappeared.

docs.title: Jain's stone
docs.text:
Jain discovered that her mysterious stone is one of a pair of Sending Stones.

  • It can be used once per day.
  • The other stone is held by someone else.
  • Jain tried contacting whoever has the matching stone.
  • No one answered.

Elisandra also returned Jain's Necklace of Disguise.

docs.title: Pyrite's Booty
docs.text:
We sold our accumulated treasure, including Lord Waterford's jeweled walking stick.

Total received: 4,000 gp.

  • Bia: 1,000 gp
  • Cadric: 1,100 gp
  • Jain: 1,100 gp
  • Elisandra: 1,100 gp

Bia's share was smaller because I already had additional gold from the crypt beneath the Waterford mausoleum.

docs.title: Hammerbarn
docs.text:
At the blacksmith:

  • Bia sold her extra greataxe for 27 gp.
  • Jain left her shortsword to be imbued with silver.
  • The process will take one week.
  • The blacksmith can only work on one weapon at a time.
  • Cadric considered leaving his sword but decided against it because his wouldn't be ready until another week after Jain's.

docs.title: Atom's Arcana
docs.text:
Lots of magical things we couldn't afford.

Cadric found one he could.

  • Eversmoking Bottle
  • Cost: 950 gp

docs.title: Rudolph Van Richten
docs.text:
Jennifer and Lori had recommended that we visit Rudolph Van Richten, a monster hunter and occult expert who operates an herbalist shop in Mordenshire.

When we arrived, we found his employee Beatrice injured outside.

  • Beatrice had gone inside to open the shop.
  • Something attacked her.
  • Elisandra went inside to investigate.
  • A shadowy black panther attacked Elisandra and knocked her unconscious.
  • After we revived her, Elisandra remained outside with Beatrice.
  • Bia, Cadric, and Jain entered the shop.

Inside:

  • There was blood on the floor.
  • The shadow panther continued appearing and disappearing.
  • A small, wiry shadow creature threw a flask at Jain and hit her in the back of the head.
  • An unseen force on the stairs tried to stop Jain from going upstairs.
  • Jain got through.
  • Bia followed.
  • Cadric had more trouble, so Bia pulled him up with a rope.

docs.title: Upstairs
docs.text:
Van Richten's living quarters contained research about the different domains of Ravenloft.

Jain found:

  • Van Richten's Guide to Ravenloft
  • a scroll
  • a strange mummified cat covered in markings and broken into two pieces

Jain tried putting the cat back together.

Of course she did.

In the master bedroom, we found Rudolph Van Richten frozen in mid-step. He couldn't move, but his eyes could.

By asking questions and having him move his eyes left or right, we determined that the scroll Jain found could help him.

The scroll contained Protection from Evil and Good.

Cadric read it.

Van Richten could move again.

docs.title: The mummified cat
docs.text:
Van Richten explained that the mummified cat was responsible for the creatures in the shop.

We took it to a ritual chamber in his basement.

  • Van Richten placed the mummy inside a magical circle.
  • He had to concentrate on a ritual.
  • Our job was to protect him.
  • Shadows gathered above the mummy and formed the giant black panther.
  • We fought it while Van Richten continued chanting.
  • Cadric was knocked unconscious.
  • The ritual succeeded.
  • The panther dissolved back into the mummy.
  • The two broken pieces of the cat fused together again.

Afterward, we revived Cadric and had tea.

docs.title: Lord Godfroy
docs.text:
Van Richten knows quite a bit about Godfroy.

  • Godfroy can control ghosts who died after him.
  • The ghosts apparently have some freedom in how they interpret his orders.
  • Henry Loust was Godfroy's head butler while alive and is probably subject to this control.
  • Lady Estella Godfroy opposes Godfroy.
  • She remains trapped at Griffin Hill after one of Godfroy's experiments killed her.
  • Godfroy's ghosts can move through walls.
  • They can observe people without being seen.

Something to remember while visiting Griffin Hill.

docs.title: Mist Horror
docs.text:
Jain described what happened to her in the Mists outside Candle Cross.

Van Richten believes the creature she encountered may have been a Mist Horror.

  • Incorporeal predator.
  • Uses fear to lure victims.
  • Can apparently take forms meaningful to its victims.

docs.title: Traveling through the Mists
docs.text:
Van Richten explained:

  • Talismans associated with specific domains can help travelers reach those domains.
  • A Mist Wanderer can eventually find a route to a named destination.
  • The route may not be safe.
  • The route may not be direct.

Jain is a Mist Wanderer.

docs.title: Glim Brightstone
docs.text:
We told Van Richten about the strange machine beneath Candle Cross.

He thought it might be connected to Glim Brightstone and may have contained a Glim battery.

This sounds similar to the technology we found in the laboratory near the Black Lantern Inn, where we left Cedgewick.

Van Richten has also heard rumors about the apparatus Godfroy is seeking.

Depending on which rumors are true, it may:

  • allow someone to travel safely through the Mists;
  • remove a soul from one body and place it into another;
  • possibly do something similar on a much larger scale.

None of this makes me feel better about Godfroy wanting it.

docs.title: Gifts from Van Richten
docs.text:
Before we left, Van Richten gave us:

  • Lantern of Reveal
  • Stone of Good Luck
  • 6 vials of holy water
  • 4 wooden stakes
  • Tarokka deck

Van Richten also agreed to make silver canine caps for Jain.

docs.title: The breath of the dead
docs.text:
That evening, Cadric performed at the Blackcard.

His original song received mild applause.

The familiar songs went much better.

Henry Loust was in the audience. Jain noticed him watching us and sat beside him.

"Jain."

"Henry."

Henry told us that Godfroy knew we had reached Mordenshire and expected us to make time for him.

Meanwhile, a thick fog rolled into town.

The locals call it:

The breath of the dead.

Jain and Elisandra started back toward the Salty Dog.

Jain noticed a strange flickering light somewhere in the fog.

Then she smelled blood.

Elisandra returned to the Blackcard. Bia joined Jain.

We followed the smell toward the docks.

docs.title: Madeline's murder
docs.text:
We found Madeline, one of the Blackcard's barmaids.

She was dead.

  • Her throat had been slit.
  • Her tongue had been removed.
  • A chunk of hair had been torn from the back of her head.
  • Blood and skin were beneath her fingernails.
  • She had fought back.
  • The wounds were clean.
  • It appeared the murderer had grabbed her from behind.

Jain found a trail of blood leading toward the sanatorium.

Bia went to the Salty Dog looking for help and then ran to the garrison.

When I returned with guards, Jain was gone.

Naturally.

docs.title: Jain investigates
docs.text:
Jain followed the blood trail toward the sanatorium.

A guard told her that he had heard something moving in the bushes.

Jain's conclusion:

"Well, fuck, that's the murderer."

She went into the bushes.

Two sanatorium guards eventually searched with her.

They found:

  • footprints leading from pavement into the grass;
  • a bloody dagger approximately six inches long.

The guards considered that enough and told Jain to return to the docks.

Jain disagreed.

"You guys kind of fucking suck, no offense, but this is what I'm good at. Can you let me do this?"

"You don't work for the city of Mordenshire."

"Do I need to work for the city to avenge someone's death?"

Apparently she did.

docs.title: "It wasn't me"
docs.text:
The guards questioned Jain at the docks.

Her summary:

"Smell blood, body dark, body dead, blood, blood trail, follow blood trail, find weapon."

This did not make her look less suspicious.

The following morning, two guards collected Jain from the Salty Dog and took her to the garrison to speak with Captain Kilm O'Connell.

Jain explained everything again.

She also pointed out that she had told the sanatorium guard before going into the bushes.

"Wouldn't it be more weird if I just ran into the bushes without saying anything?"

She reminded O'Connell:

"I played a critical role in this case."

O'Connell asked:

"You understand how you look, right?"

Jain understood.

"I didn't do it."

Fortunately, O'Connell already knew that.

Madeline was the fourth murder victim.

Jain had only arrived in Mordenshire the previous day.

"Oh, do you know it wasn't me then?"

Yes.

She still looked "suspicious as shit."

docs.title: The sanatorium
docs.text:
Captain O'Connell needed people to investigate Mordenshire's sanatorium.

The facility operates with very little oversight from the town.

We later met with:

  • Captain Kilm O'Connell
  • Mayor Alice Weathermay

The sanatorium is controlled by Dr. Caroline Resdonna.

  • Resdonna brings in outside researchers and staff.
  • The sanatorium largely avoids town oversight.
  • O'Connell wants to know what is happening inside.
  • We also need to determine whether the sanatorium is connected to the murders.

docs.title: Our covers
docs.text:
• Jain - Patient
  • Elisandra - Patient
  • Bia - Janitor
  • Cadric - Groundskeeper

The operation begins in three days.

The paperwork for Bia and Cadric should be ready by then.

docs.title: The EC Light
docs.text:
Cadric and Elisandra designed a reusable magical light.

The EC Light consists of:

  • a copper outer tube;
  • a silver inner component enchanted with Continual Flame;
  • a removable cap that blocks the light when it isn't needed.

They commissioned two at Hammerbarn:

  • one for Cadric;
  • one for Elisandra.

Cadric also ordered a custom utility belt from the tannery with:

  • a holster for the EC Light;
  • a special pouch for his Eversmoking Bottle;
  • a design that allows smoke to escape while keeping the bottle secured.

Elisandra ordered a utility belt with a holster for her EC Light.

docs.title: Items in progress

docs.title: House on Griffin Hill
docs.text:
We finally went to the House on Griffin Hill.

The estate is just outside Mordenshire.

  • Tall wrought-iron gates.
  • Gates opened after Bia announced that Henry Loust had invited us.
  • Immaculate grounds.
  • Elaborate hedges and topiaries.
  • Gardeners/workers sometimes appeared at the edge of our vision.
  • When we looked directly at them, no one was there.
  • There was a large area of recently disturbed and compacted earth.

Henry said they were expanding the manor.

Inside:

  • The sitting room was strangely dusty compared with the grounds.
  • Cadric found a piano and played it.
  • Elisandra found a leather-bound journal connected to Glim.
  • It was the only journal in the bookcase that wasn't covered in dust.
  • Jain found a decanter containing what appeared to be pure alcohol.
  • Jain heard a metallic scraping/digging noise beneath the floor.
  • Cadric could feel vibrations.

Something is happening beneath Griffin Hill.

docs.title: Lord Godfroy's job
docs.text:
Godfroy needs "capable mortal hands."

He wants us to investigate Glim Brightstone and locate a more powerful Glim battery.

He gave us three leads.

docs.title: Welkspring House - Echo Island
docs.text:
• One of Glim's friends wrote that Welkspring House was a safe haven.
  • Strange blue writing at the house apparently prevents ghosts from entering.

docs.title: Cauldron of Tepist
docs.text:
• Contains fountains associated with resurrection.
  • Godfroy believes they may have inspired part of Glim's apparatus.

docs.title: Falkovnia
docs.text:
We need to find Mikhail Hatzimvas.

  • He established a hospital near a mountain.
  • He helps people suffering from the region's undead affliction.
  • He may know where Glim went.
  • He may know what Glim was working on.

docs.title: Payment
docs.text:
Godfroy wants us to investigate all three leads and find the larger battery.

Payment:

15,000 gp per party member.

We leave in one week.

docs.title: Cadric's borrowed sword
docs.text:
Cadric's ordinary sword won't be useful against ghosts.

Since he didn't leave it at Hammerbarn to be silvered, Godfroy agreed to lend him a +1 shortsword.

Henry brought the sword to Cadric.

Good news:

It isn't cursed.

Bad news:

Godfroy can scry on Cadric through it.

docs.title: Alenta
docs.text:
Elderly Gnome innkeeper at the Blackcard.

Keeps an old grimoire behind the front desk.

docs.title: Menda

Innkeeper at the Salty Dog.

Met Jain and Elisandra as "Jainisandra."

docs.title: Beatrice

Employee at Van Richten's Herbalist.

Monster hunter and occult expert.

Runs an herbalist shop in Mordenshire and knows considerably more about the Mists, Godfroy, Glim, and Ravenloft than most people we've met.

Barmaid at the Blackcard.

Fourth known victim of the Mordenshire murderer.

Mayor of Mordenshire.

Mother of Jennifer and Lori.

Working with Captain O'Connell on the sanatorium investigation.

docs.text:
Controls Mordenshire's sanatorium.

Brings in outside researchers and staff and operates with little town oversight.

Dreadlord at the House on Griffin Hill.

Hired Ravenlost to investigate three leads connected to Glim Brightstone and retrieve a larger Glim battery.

Payment: 15,000 gp each.

Established a hospital in Falkovnia for people suffering from the region's undead affliction.

One of Godfroy's leads for locating Glim or learning more about his work.

docs.title: Advancement
docs.text: Ravenlost reached Level 4.

docs.title: Adventure at a glance
docs.text: Item Details Location Mordenshire Sanatorium Goal Investigate the sanatorium and determine whether it is connected to the murders in Mordenshire Party covers Bia and Jain — patients; Cadric — groundskeeper; Elisandra — janitor "Sandra Korn" Key NPCs Dr. Caroline Resdonna, Dr. Dave, Dr. Van Larder, Peter, Helen, Cookie, Belinda Patients Randolph, Janice, Robert, Wendel, Trashcan Major discoveries Wendel disappeared into the ICU; strange writing hidden throughout his old room; dissected brain and "GE" clue in the morgue; third floor is restricted; orderlies obey Dr. Caroline's voice Current situation Dr. Caroline poisoned and injured; Jain loose in the ICU; Cadric disguised as Dr. Caroline; party still unarmed inside the sanatorium Cliffhanger Dr. Dave cast Fireball. I failed my save and took 18 damage.

docs.title: Ready to roll
docs.text:
We returned to the mayor's residence after meeting with Lord Godfroy and agreed to investigate the sanatorium.

The mayor already had employee badges for Cadric and Elisandra. The plan:

  • Cadric: Groundskeeper
  • Elisandra: Janitor, using the name Sandra Korn
  • Jain: Patient, after causing a disturbance at the docks
  • Bia: Patient, after warning everyone in town about an approaching undead army

We left our weapons and armor at the garrison before going in the next day.

We had one goal. Investigate what was happening at the sanatorium.

What could go wrong?

docs.title: The sanatorium
docs.text: The sanatorium has three floors and a basement.

docs.title: First floor
docs.text:
• Intake area
  • Lower-security patients
  • Nurses' station
  • Common areas
  • Kitchen
  • Staff areas
  • Access to the grounds/farm
  • I was initially placed here as a lower-security patient.

docs.title: Second floor
docs.text:
• Intake area
  • Higher-security patients
  • Jain was placed in a cell here.
  • ICU
  • Nurses' station
  • Lobby with a large window overlooking Mordenshire
  • Dr. Caroline has access to the ICU.
  • Dr. Dave also works in the ICU.
  • Dr. Van Larder does not work in the ICU.
  • I was allowed on this floor to "watch" for the undead army.

docs.title: Third floor
docs.text:
• Off limits.
  • Cadric reached the locked gate but didn't get beyond it.
  • We still don't know what's up there.

docs.title: Basement
docs.text:
• Boiler
  • Morgue
  • Janitor's quarters
  • Elisandra is responsible for tending the boiler several times a day.
  • The boiler helps power the elevator.
  • Helen is her boss.

docs.title: Dr. Caroline Resdonna
docs.text:
Currently in charge of the sanatorium.

  • Took over the sanatorium with Dr. Dave approximately 18 months ago.
  • Remodeled part of the former high-security wing into the ICU.
  • Has her quarters on the 3rd floor.
  • Has access to the ICU.
  • Eats separately from the other staff.
  • Questioned Jain inside the ICU.
  • Cadric successfully drugged her stew with hemlock.
  • Jain attacked and choked her after escaping her restraints.
  • The orderlies respond to her commands.

docs.title: Dr. Dave
docs.text:
Arrived with Dr. Caroline approximately 18 months ago.

  • Dr. Van Larder said Dr. Dave and Dr. Caroline are old friends.
  • Works in/accesses the ICU.
  • Spoke with me about the "undead army" and allowed me to work outside on defenses.
  • Was involved when Jain was taken to the ICU.
  • Appeared from deeper inside the ICU during the confrontation with Dr. Caroline.
  • Cast Fireball at us at the end of the session.

docs.title: Dr. Van Larder
docs.text:
Elderly doctor who has worked at the sanatorium for 43 years.

  • Doesn't work in or have access to the ICU.
  • Told me that only Dr. Caroline and Dr. Dave go into the ICU.
  • Seemed strangely unconcerned by the condition of Wendel's old room.

docs.title: Peter
docs.text:
Night watchman.

  • Cadric's boss.
  • Showed Cadric his quarters and explained his groundskeeping duties.

docs.title: Helen
docs.text:
Nighttime janitor.

  • Trained Elisandra on her duties.
  • Told Elisandra that the ICU should only be cleaned when specifically requested.

Cookie

Sanatorium cook.

  • Cadric befriended him.
  • Asked Cadric to get butter from town.
  • Was making molasses cookies.
  • Helped Cadric learn Dr. Caroline's eating habits.
  • Cadric used his kitchen access to drug Dr. Caroline's stew.
  • Cadric planned to also drug 4 cookies and deliver those to nurses and other nighttime staff.

docs.title: Belinda
docs.text:
Intake nurse.

  • Handled Jain's intake.
  • Put Jain in "Wendel's old room."

docs.title: Randolph
docs.text:
Lower-security patient.

  • Has been at the sanatorium for about two years.
  • From Mordent.

docs.title: Janice
docs.text:
Lower-security patient.

  • Has been at the sanatorium for about three years.
  • From Mordent.
  • Told me about the ICU and the changes Dr. Caroline made to the sanatorium.

docs.title: Robert
docs.text:
Lower-security patient.

  • Has been at the sanatorium for about six months.
  • Originally from Barovia.
  • Says he became lost in the Mists and eventually arrived here.

docs.title: Wendel
docs.text:
Previous occupant of Jain's room.

  • Was taken to the ICU approximately one week ago.
  • Hasn't returned.
  • His room was much more damaged than the other patient rooms.
  • Writing was hidden beneath the padding, floorboards, and other surfaces.

docs.title: Trashcan
docs.text:
• A patient who lives inside a trashcan and has apparently been at the sanatorium for more than two years.
  • Jain discovered that she could communicate with him by asking yes-or-no questions:
  • Trash = yes
  • Can = no
  • Trashcan confirmed that he had been at the sanatorium for more than two years and that he collects trash.
  • Jain told him that she wanted to escape and asked if he could help her get out. Trashcan shuffled closer to her cell. After Jain unsuccessfully tried to pick her lock without tools, Trashcan said, "Trash," reached inside his trashcan, and produced a lock. It wasn't particularly useful, but he appeared to understand what Jain wanted and attempted to help.
  • Dr. Dave later told Sandra that the staff have been trying for years to get Trashcan out of the trashcan, but that he becomes "a different being" when outside it.
  • Still unclear: What exactly Trashcan is, why he refuses to leave the trashcan, and how freely he can move around the sanatorium.

docs.title: The orderlies
docs.text:
The orderlies are enormous bald men, some nearly as large as me.

Things we noticed:

  • Rarely or never speak.
  • Show almost no emotional response.
  • Extremely strong.
  • Follow instructions immediately.
  • Seem to respond to Dr. Caroline's voice.
  • Jain successfully imitated Dr. Caroline and ordered them to stop.
  • They obeyed her.

Important: They may be responding to Dr. Caroline's voice, not necessarily Dr. Caroline herself.

docs.title: Wendel's room
docs.text:
Jain was placed in Wendel's old room.

It was noticeably more damaged than the other rooms. Jain began pulling away padding, floorboards, and pieces of the walls.

The same two messages appeared repeatedly:

"She will come visit you."

"No, he won't."

Some of the writing appeared to have been made with blood and other substances.

We don't know who she or he refers to.

docs.title: The ICU
docs.text:
Other patients warned me:

"You generally don't come back."

Wendel was taken there a week ago and hasn't returned.

I briefly saw through the ICU door when Dr. Caroline entered. The first room looked very different from the rest of the sanatorium:

  • Oak paneling
  • Leather chaise
  • Chair beside it
  • Looked more like a therapist's office than a hospital room
  • Another door led farther into the ICU
  • Jain was eventually taken there and restrained on the chaise.

Dr. Caroline questioned her while eating dinner.

Dr. Dave later emerged from a room farther inside the ICU.

We still don't know what's behind the second door.

docs.title: The morgue
docs.text:
Elisandra discovered the recently autopsied body of a woman in the basement morgue.

  • Skull had been opened.
  • Brain had been cut into sections.
  • An anatomical drawing of a brain was nearby.
  • Part of the left hemisphere was marked: GE

We don't know what GE means or what was done to the woman's brain.

docs.title: Talking about "gardening"
docs.text:
I managed to get outside by convincing Dr. Dave that I needed to prepare defenses against the undead army.

I was put to work on the grounds.

Cadric and I then spoke to each other in Halfling, pretending to discuss gardening and farming techniques so the orderlies and other patients wouldn't understand us.

This gave Cadric a way to update me on what everyone had discovered and his plan for that night.

docs.title: Cadric's plan
docs.text:
Cadric left the sanatorium after his shift to get butter for Cookie.

He also stopped at the garrison and retrieved his remaining hemlock.

He successfully smuggled it back into the sanatorium.

The plan was to:

  1. Drug Dr. Caroline's dinner.
  2. Prepare three drugged molasses cookies for other staff.
  3. Wait until later that night.
  4. Investigate the restricted areas while Dr. Caroline was incapacitated.
  5. Help Jain and me get out as needed.

Cadric successfully added hemlock to Dr. Caroline's stew.

The cookies never happened.

docs.title: Jain had other plans
docs.text:
Jain woke inside the ICU restrained while Dr. Caroline ate the poisoned stew.

Dr. Caroline questioned her, but Jain refused to answer.

Eventually, Dr. Caroline passed out.

Jain:

  • Dislocated her thumb.
  • Escaped her restraints.
  • Attacked Dr. Caroline when she regained consciousness.
  • Choked Dr. Caroline.
  • Caused Dr. Caroline to scream before the nighttime plan was ready.

Because it wasn't lights-out yet, I was still allowed in the upstairs lobby.

Cadric, Elisandra, and I converged on the second floor after hearing Dr. Caroline scream.

docs.title: Two Dr. Carolines
docs.text:
As the orderlies approached, Jain imitated Dr. Caroline's voice and ordered them to stop.

It worked.

Cadric then:

  1. Drank his Potion of Growth.
  2. Grew to approximately Dr. Caroline's height.
  3. Cast Disguise Self to look like Dr. Caroline.
  4. Broke into the ICU.

There were now two Dr. Carolines:

  • The real Dr. Caroline, being choked by Jain.
  • Cadric, disguised as Dr. Caroline.

Dr. Dave emerged from deeper inside the ICU and saw the situation.

He raised his hand.

A small orange mote, about the size of a marble, appeared and streaked toward the doorway.

Fireball.

That's where we stopped.

docs.title: Things we still need to figure out
docs.text:
• What's actually happening inside the ICU?
  • What's behind the second ICU door?
  • What's on the third floor?
  • What happened to Wendel?
  • Who are "she" and "he" in the messages in Wendel's room?
  • What does GE mean?
  • Why was the dead woman's brain dissected?
  • Who was the woman in the morgue?
  • What are the orderlies?
  • Why do the orderlies obey Dr. Caroline's voice?
  • Can someone other than Jain imitate Dr. Caroline and control them?
  • What exactly are Dr. Caroline and Dr. Dave doing?
  • Why doesn't Dr. Van Larder ever enter the ICU?
  • How much does Dr. Van Larder know?
  • Why did Dr. Caroline go toward Peter's house?
  • What is Trashcan's deal?
  • What happened to the other patients who went into the ICU?

docs.title: Items / money
docs.text:
• Sent two letters home.
  • Sent 1 platinum piece home.
  • Cost to send the two letters: 4 gp
  • Weapons and armor are currently at the garrison.
  • Cadric retrieved the remaining hemlock from the garrison.
  • Cadric used his Potion of Growth.
  • Dr. Caroline consumed the hemlock in her stew.

docs.title: Important for next time
docs.text:
We are unarmed.

Our weapons and armor are still at the garrison.

I failed my save and took 18 damage.

Dr. Caroline is injured and is being held/choked by Jain.

Cadric is still disguised as Dr. Caroline.

Jain had demonstrated that the orderlies would obey her imitation of Dr. Caroline's voice.

Dr. Dave is present.

We're still inside the sanatorium.

This could be going better.

docs.title: Bia's journal
docs.text:
Pretending an undead army was coming seemed like a good idea at the time.

It got me into the sanatorium. It got me upstairs. It even got me outside, after I convinced a doctor that I needed to help defend Mordenshire. I was then allowed to discuss "gardening" with Cadric.

So really, that part of the plan worked perfectly.

Cadric had a plan too. His involved hemlock, stew, cookies, and waiting until everyone was asleep.

Jain's plan was different.

Now Dr. Caroline has been poisoned, Jain is choking her, Cadric looks like Dr. Caroline, the giant bald orderlies will apparently listen to anyone who sounds like Dr. Caroline, and Dr. Dave just threw a fireball at us.

I miss the undead army.

docs.title: Bia's notes - It's been a long week
Adventure at a glance
docs.text:
Ravenlost's investigation of the sanatorium came to a fiery conclusion. Dr. Caroline died, Dr. Dave was captured, and the party discovered evidence of experiments involving brain surgery, memory loss, and susceptibility to commands. They also uncovered a connection between the sanatorium's expansion and Lord Godfroy.

After reporting their findings to Mordenshire's authorities, Ravenlost spent several days recovering, collecting equipment, and researching Godfroy's three leads. Information from Gilda Haywood pointed them toward Osgood Escar, a botanist who had known Glim Brightstone and owned Welkspring House on Echo Island.

The journey involved an unusual boat crew, a storm, an overnight stay with Shauncey, and a shortcut through a forest inhabited by hostile plant creatures.

At Welkspring House, Ravenlost encountered an automaton reminiscent of Cedgewick and finally met Osgood. After an uncomfortable conversation about their relationship with Godfroy, Osgood reluctantly invited them inside.

Ravenlost is now inside Welkspring House, hoping to learn more about Glim while keeping dangerous information out of Godfroy's hands.

docs.title: The sanatorium — fire, escape, and Dr. Caroline
docs.text: The session resumed in the ICU immediately after Dr. Dave's Fireball. The sanatorium was on fire, Dr. Caroline was unconscious, and the party was scattered across the upper floor.

docs.title: The fight in the ICU
docs.text:
• Jain was holding an unconscious Dr. Caroline. She dragged her out of the flames rather than leaving her to burn, although she also bit Caroline's cheek.
  • Bia pursued Dr. Dave through the ICU.
  • Cadric, still enlarged and disguised as Dr. Caroline, used his appearance to command the orderlies.
  • Elisandra cast Bless on Bia, Jain, and Trashcan and helped deal with the fire.
  • Trashcan attempted to unlock patient rooms and free the people trapped inside.
  • Dr. Dave hid behind a reinforced door. Cadric attempted Hold Person, but Dave resisted.

docs.title: Wendel and the orderlies
docs.text:
The party encountered an enormous, scarred man who appeared to be Wendel, the patient who had disappeared into the ICU.

  • Wendel initially attacked Cadric because Cadric looked like Dr. Caroline.
  • Cadric ordered two orderlies to restrain Wendel, but Wendel killed them.
  • Once Cadric dropped his disguise, Wendel became less hostile.
  • Wendel had extensive scars and appeared to have been subjected to Dr. Caroline's experiments.
  • The party eventually gained his cooperation through food, including Cookie's cookies.

Important distinction: Although Wendel had undergone some form of experimentation, we have no evidence that the procedures successfully made him susceptible to commands, as they had the orderlies.

docs.title: Dr. Caroline's death
docs.text:
Jain later discovered that Dr. Caroline had stopped breathing. She checked her pulse and considered whether she was supposed to heal her, but Caroline died before the guards arrived.

Jain dressed Caroline's body so the guards would not find her naked.

This left Ravenlost without the opportunity to question Dr. Caroline directly about her research or her arrangement with Godfroy.

docs.title: Dr. Dave's capture
docs.text:
Dr. Dave was eventually captured after Cadric successfully used Suggestion to make him surrender.

  • Dave was badly burned and required medical attention.
  • Unlike the orderlies and other patients, Dave appeared to be a willing aide in Dr. Caroline's work.
  • He knew Wendel and had access to the ICU.
  • He was uncooperative when questioned after the spell ended.
  • The authorities took custody of him.

docs.title: The patients
docs.text:
• Ravenlost helped get patients out of danger during the fire.
  • Trashcan disappeared during the confusion.
  • Wendel survived and was later allowed to stay in Dr. Caroline's former quarters, with access to the garden.
  • Dr. Goth, the party's nickname for another doctor, helped care for Wendel.

docs.title: What we found in Dr. Caroline's rooms
docs.text:
After the fighting in the ICU, Ravenlost searched Dr. Caroline's quarters for evidence of what had been happening inside the sanatorium.

Control: A Roadmap

The most important discovery was a book titled Control: A Roadmap, which helped explain the disturbing behavior of the orderlies and the condition of several patients.

The research appeared to involve surgically altering people to make them more susceptible to suggestions or commands.

  • The orderlies had similar scars on the tops of their heads, suggesting they had undergone the same procedure.
  • The orderlies responded to commands from someone they believed was Dr. Caroline, as Cadric had demonstrated while disguised as her.
  • Wendel had extensive surgical scars, but he did not exhibit the same obedient behavior.
  • The experiments appeared to involve repeated attempts to achieve a particular result.

What we know: The sanatorium was being used for experiments involving behavioral control, and the orderlies appeared to be successfully altered subjects.

What we don't know: Exactly how the procedures worked, how many people were experimented on, or whether the effects could be reversed.

docs.title: Dr. Edgar Iskander
docs.text:
Jain and Elisandra found several items connecting Dr. Caroline to Dr. Edgar Iskander.

  • Doctor's robes: Found in a locked chest, embroidered with Dr. Edgar Iskander's name and associated with Locust Branch Hospital in Crawford.
  • Pencil sketch: Depicted a man holding a young child. On the back was written: “To my dear star, I’ll make the world a safer place for you.”
  • Research journal: Control: A Roadmap, written by Dr. Edgar Iskander approximately 40 years earlier. The handwriting matched the message on the sketch.

The journal indicated that Edgar had lost his funding at Locust Branch Hospital after a surgery went wrong and a patient became violent.

Our theory: Edgar was Dr. Caroline's father, and she continued his research. The evidence is compelling, but we haven't confirmed their relationship.

docs.title: Dr. Caroline's patient records
docs.text:
The records contained numerous names, many crossed out or marked as failed experiments or unsuitable candidates.

Patient What we learned Wendel Listed among the experimental subjects; had extensive scarring Peter His name appeared in the records Trashcan His entry contained several question marks Anne Recorded as having died during surgery Jain Described as a “Lupine — promising candidate”

Dr. Caroline had apparently identified Jain as a potential subject almost immediately after her admission.

docs.title: Lord Godfroy's involvement
docs.text:
The party discovered architectural plans for the sanatorium's remodeled wing, including the restricted ICU.

Lord Godfroy had privately funded the addition.

This was the first concrete evidence connecting him to the sanatorium's activities.

Later, Henry Loust confirmed that Dr. Caroline and Godfroy had an arrangement: Godfroy financed the new wing in exchange for Caroline supplying things he needed.

Ravenlost suspects Caroline intended to perfect Edgar's research and provide the results to Godfroy.

However, we still don't know exactly what Godfroy requested, how much he knew about the experiments, or how he intends to use the research.

docs.title: Questions to investigate later
docs.text:
• Was Dr. Edgar Iskander actually Dr. Caroline's father?
  • What happened to Edgar after he lost his funding at Locust Branch Hospital?
  • Can the effects of the experimental surgeries be reversed?
  • What exactly did Godfroy expect Dr. Caroline to supply?
  • Was Godfroy interested in controlling living people, or does this research serve another purpose?

docs.title: Peter and the Mordenshire murders
docs.text: After uncovering Dr. Caroline's experiments, Ravenlost still needed to solve the murders that had brought them to the sanatorium in the first place.

docs.title: The missing nightwatchman
docs.text:
Peter, the sanatorium's nightwatchman and Cadric's supervisor, had disappeared from his post.

Ravenlost investigated his quarters and discovered several suspicious details:

  • His bed appeared untouched.
  • A chair had been placed in the room.
  • A worn circular path suggested someone had been pacing repeatedly.
  • A case designed to hold seven daggers contained only five.

The missing daggers were particularly concerning given the murders around Mordenshire.

Ravenlost alerted the guards, who helped secure the area while the party followed Peter's trail.

docs.title: The confrontation at the docks
docs.text:
Peter's trail eventually led to the docks.

Before pursuing him, Ravenlost retrieved their weapons and equipment from the garrison, where they had left them before entering the sanatorium undercover.

At the docks, Peter attempted to escape.

  • Jain tried to shoot him with an arrow, but she missed and hit a drunk soldier instead.
  • Bia pursued and subdued Peter.
  • During the confrontation, Peter stabbed Bia.
  • Bia knocked Peter unconscious against a wooden piling.
  • Peter survived and was taken into custody.
  • Cadric applied some aid to the drunk sailor - Captain Jethro Fletcher.

The evidence strongly suggested that Peter was responsible for the murders, but Ravenlost had begun to suspect he might not have been acting voluntarily.

docs.title: Peter's condition
docs.text:
When questioned afterward, Peter appeared confused.

  • He remembered reporting for his night shift at the sanatorium.
  • He did not remember leaving his post.
  • He had no memory of fleeing to the docks, attacking Bia, or being captured.
  • The guards discovered surgical incisions behind his ears.

These incisions were different from the scars on the orderlies' heads, but they suggested Peter had also undergone some form of experimental surgery.

Our conclusion: Peter was almost certainly the murderer, but Dr. Caroline may have manipulated him into committing the crimes.

We don't know whether Peter was aware of his actions at the time or whether his missing memories can be recovered.

docs.title: Reporting to the authorities
docs.text: Ravenlost met with Mayor Alice Weathermay and Captain O'Connell to report what they had discovered.

docs.title: Evidence presented
docs.text:
The party explained or showed the authorities:

  • Dr. Edgar Iskander's research journal, Control: A Roadmap.
  • The experiments involving memory, aggression, and susceptibility to commands.
  • The identical surgical scars on the orderlies.
  • Peter's missing memories, surgical incisions, and connection to the murders.
  • Dr. Caroline's death and Dr. Dave's capture.
  • The architectural plans showing that Lord Godfroy financed the sanatorium's restricted wing.

Captain O'Connell confirmed that the orderlies did not speak and had identical scarring around their skulls.

The authorities also identified a deceased patient in the morgue as Anne Polk, who had been at the sanatorium for approximately three years.

docs.title: Dr. Dave's involvement
docs.text:
Dr. Dave had arrived at the sanatorium with Dr. Caroline and worked alongside her in the ICU.

Unlike Peter and the orderlies, there was no indication that Dave had been subjected to the experiments against his will.

He appeared to have participated in these experiments on patients knowingly.

Although he survived the confrontation with Ravenlost, he was badly burned and remained uncooperative when questioned.

docs.title: What happens next?
docs.text:
With Dr. Caroline dead and Dr. Dave in custody, the sanatorium's leadership had effectively collapsed.

The authorities now had evidence of serious wrongdoing, but several questions remained unanswered:

  • How many patients had been experimented on?
  • How many had died?
  • What would happen to the surviving patients?
  • Could Peter be held responsible for murders he might have committed under someone else's control?
  • Would Dr. Dave eventually reveal what he knew?
  • Would the authorities investigate Godfroy's financial involvement?

Ravenlost had solved the immediate murder mystery, but the investigation had exposed something considerably larger.

docs.title: Mordenshire — rewards and recovery
docs.text: With the sanatorium investigation concluded, Ravenlost finally had a few days to recover, collect their belongings, and prepare for their next assignment.

docs.title: Mayor Alice's rewards
docs.text:
Mayor Alice thanked Ravenlost for their work investigating the murders and the sanatorium.

Three party members received magical items:

Character Reward Notes Jain Periapt of Health A magical item that protects against disease Elisandra Pearl of Power Allows its bearer to regain an expended spell slot, subject to the item's limitations Cadric Aurum and Argentum A matched pair of magical daggers Bia — Didn’t receive a magical item

Aurum and Argentum description:

  • This gold and silver set of daggers seem ordinary when used on their own but become magical when used together.
  • You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage roles made with these daggers while you hold one of them in each hand.
  • When Cadric engages in two-weapon fighting using these daggers, he can add his ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.
  • In addition, if Cadric hits the same target with both daggers in the same round, the target takes an extra 1d4 piercing damage from the second attack, and the target can’t use its reaction until the end of Cadric’s turn.

docs.title: Checking on old friends
docs.text:
Bia visited Randal, Janice, and Robert, the three former sanatorium patients she had helped.

All three had found work and were settling into life outside the institution.

Between them, their jobs included work at the Blackard, running errands at the market, and working in a wheat field.

Bia gave each of them 1 gp to help them get started.

docs.title: Cadric's new song
docs.text:
Cadric returned to performing at the Blackard.

His latest song featured a wandering halfling whose adventures were beginning to sound suspiciously familiar.

One verse even involved an orc with a very large axe.

The chorus included:

With the wandering halfling, wherever he may roam, He'll find a warm fire and he'll call it his home. With a song in his heart and a coin in his shoe, He'll steal your heart first and all of your silver too.

Cadric performed over four nights, earning a total of 16 gp in silver.

His performances also featured magical imagery accompanying the music.

docs.title: Jain's discovery
docs.text:
Jain spent some time exploring the cliffs overlooking the sea.

From her vantage point, she spotted something remarkable offshore.

Trashcan was sitting on a trash barge.

He appeared perfectly content.

Jain did not tell the others.

As far as the rest of Ravenlost knew, Trashcan had simply disappeared during the sanatorium evacuation.

docs.title: Elisandra's raven
docs.text:
Elisandra spent some of the downtime with her new raven, attempting to teach it to speak.

Whether the raven would eventually become conversational remained to be seen.

docs.title: Returning to Old Books
docs.text: Four days after commissioning research into Welkspring House, Ravenlost returned to Old Books to see what Gilda Haywood had discovered.

docs.title: Gilda's research
docs.text:
Gilda had collected a considerable amount of information about Osgood Escar, the owner of Welkspring House.

Subject Findings Name Osgood Escar Occupation Botanist and researcher Residence Welkspring House, Echo Island Property history Purchased Welkspring House 73 years ago Research Plants, including poisonous species, collected during travels through the Mists Connection to Glim Osgood and Glim Brightstone knew each other and appeared to have been close Where they met Borca Current status No record of Osgood's death Godfroy connection Gilda found no evidence of a direct relationship

docs.title: Osgood and Glim
docs.text:
Several of Osgood's books contained affectionate dedications to Glim Brightstone.

The language suggested that Glim had been an important part of Osgood's life and work.

Ravenlost wondered whether their relationship might have been more than a professional friendship, but nothing confirmed that theory.

The research also raised an obvious question: If Osgood was human and purchased Welkspring House 73 years ago, how was he still alive?

docs.title: Cadric's interest in hemlock
docs.text:
Gilda's research also identified hemlock growing along the northwestern coast of Echo Island.

Cadric was particularly interested in obtaining some.

Given his recent activities at the sanatorium, that probably surprised nobody.

docs.title: Preparing to leave Mordenshire
docs.text:
Before departing, Ravenlost dealt with their remaining equipment and commissions.

  • Jain had obtained silver caps for her canine teeth from Rudolph Van Richten.
  • Jain had also commissioned a silvered shortsword from the blacksmith.
  • Cadric had acquired Arum and Argentum.
  • The magical shortsword loaned to Cadric by Godfroy remained inside the Bag of Holding, where Ravenlost hoped it would prevent Godfroy from using the weapon to scry on Cadric.

Ravenlost still had three leads from Godfroy:

  1. Welkspring House, on Echo Island.
  2. The Cauldron of Tempest.
  3. Mikhail Hatzimvas, in Falkovnia.

They chose Welkspring House first because it was relatively close, could be reached without traveling through the Mists, and offered a possible connection to Glim.

And Cadric wanted hemlock.

That was apparently enough to settle the matter.

docs.title: The voyage to Echo Island
docs.text: Ravenlost arranged passage to Echo Island aboard The Fletcher, a small sailing vessel captained by Jethro Fletcher.

docs.title: Jethro and Gobbo
docs.text:
The party found The Fletcher at the Mordenshire docks, but Jethro wasn't aboard.

They eventually located him at the Seven Seas, a tavern popular with sailors.

  • Jethro was passed out at the bar, holding a mug.
  • Gobbo, a small green goblin, was sitting nearby on a stool.
  • Gobbo introduced himself as Jethro's first mate.
  • When asked to wake the captain, Gobbo kicked Jethro with both feet, knocking him off his stool and onto the floor.

Jethro recognized Cadric, who had previously healed his injured leg.

He was also acquainted with Jain, but he didn’t know it. She had shot him.

docs.title: Negotiating passage
docs.text:
Jethro agreed to take Ravenlost to Echo Island.

  • Vessel: The Fletcher, approximately 30 feet long, with a single mast.
  • Destination: The southern shore of Echo Island.
  • Estimated travel time: Approximately 12 hours, weather permitting.
  • Limitation: Jethro refused to approach Welkspring House itself.
  • Payment: Jethro initially offered passage for free because Ravenlost had helped him previously.

The party insisted on paying and agreed to provide six cases of liquor.

Each case cost 6 sp, for a total of 36 sp.

The payment arrangement was:

When Cases Before departure 1 Upon arrival at Echo Island 2 When Jethro returned to collect Ravenlost 3 Total 6

Jethro and Gobbo would return to pick up Ravenlost when the party was ready to leave.

docs.title: The storm
docs.text:
The first half of the voyage was relatively uneventful.

Then the weather deteriorated.

A powerful storm struck The Fletcher, forcing everyone to help keep the small boat under control.

  • Bia held one of the main lines, although she needed Jethro to point out which rope he meant.
  • Gobbo ended up hanging from the end of the rope Bia was holding.
  • Jain and Elisandra helped steady the rudder.
  • Cadric attempted to encourage everyone with a sea shanty, but his performance wasn't particularly effective.
  • Jethro managed to guide the boat safely to the southern dock.

Despite the storm, everyone survived the crossing.

docs.title: Meeting Shauncey
docs.text:
Ravenlost arrived at a small dock on Echo Island's southern shore.

The area contained a few buildings, fishing boats, and cliffs overlooking the water.

An older man named Shauncey, wearing a weathered raincoat and carrying a shielded lantern, came out to help secure The Fletcher.

Shauncey offered the party shelter for the night.

When he asked why they had come to Echo Island, Ravenlost avoided mentioning their real assignment.

Jain provided an explanation:

“Grass. I'm a fan of grass, and I've heard there's exquisite grass here.”

The party also claimed to be a traveling circus troupe.

Cadric performed his new song, which Shauncey thoroughly enjoyed.

Ravenlost spent the night at Shauncey's home without incident. They did not establish a watch.

By morning, the storm had passed.

docs.title: Getting directions to Welkspring House
docs.text:
Shauncey explained that Welkspring House was approximately two hours inland, beyond a forest.

He warned Ravenlost that strange things had been happening in the woods and suggested speaking with Ava, a former groundskeeper at Welkspring House.

Ava might know more about the estate and the surrounding area.

docs.title: Ava, the former groundskeeper
docs.text:
Ravenlost found Ava working near a log cabin, chopping wood.

She was a muscular woman with short brown hair who had previously worked at Welkspring House.

docs.title: What Ava told us
docs.text:
• Ava had worked as a groundskeeper at Welkspring House.
  • She had been released from her position for her own safety and received approximately a year's wages.
  • She had not returned to the estate since leaving.
  • For roughly six months, she had occasionally glimpsed strange humanoid figures moving through the forest.
  • Some figures were small, some tall and thin, and others broader.
  • The creatures left no tracks that Ava could find.
  • She did not know exactly what they were.

Ava described two possible routes to Welkspring House:

Route Description Established path Longer, but considered safer Forest shortcut Faster, but more dangerous because of the unidentified creatures

Ravenlost chose the shortcut.

Naturally.

docs.title: The forest shortcut
docs.text:
The forest was unusually quiet.

Jain eventually spotted a humanoid figure peeking from behind a tree.

Cadric attempted to communicate using a birdcall, but something responded by firing a three-inch thorn into his neck, causing 9 piercing damage.

docs.title: The creatures
docs.text:
Ravenlost encountered several unfamiliar plant-like humanoids.

  • Smaller creatures fired sharp thorns or needles.
  • Larger creatures appeared to be composed partly of vines.
  • One larger creature restrained Bia.
  • Jain severed one creature's arm, but it regenerated.
  • Several creatures were defeated, while approximately three escaped into the forest.

The party did not pursue the fleeing creatures.

We don’t know what these creatures are or whether they have any connection to Osgood or Welkspring House.

docs.title: Reaching Welkspring
docs.text:
Approximately half an hour later, Ravenlost reached the estate's perimeter.

  • The property was enclosed by a wrought-iron fence approximately 8 feet tall.
  • Tall, carefully maintained hedges stood beyond the fence.
  • Ravenlost followed the perimeter until they found an open gate.

Before entering, Cadric pulled the thorn out of his neck.
